f2a511914d8f.en: Stockholm, October 2024. <bookmark mark='a'/> The Nobel Prize in Chemistry goes half to David Baker, for designing proteins, and half to Demis Hassabis and John Jumper of Google DeepMind, for AlphaFold, a network that predicts the shape a protein folds into. <bookmark mark='b'/> The day before, the physics prize went to John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton, for the networks of Part 20. <bookmark mark='c'/> Measuring one protein's shape could take a laboratory years; AlphaFold predicts one in minutes.
f2a511914d8f.zh: 斯德哥尔摩，2024年10月。<bookmark mark='a'/>诺贝尔化学奖一半授予大卫·贝克，表彰蛋白质设计；另一半授予谷歌DeepMind的德米斯·哈萨比斯和约翰·江珀，表彰AlphaFold，一个能预测蛋白质折叠成什么形状的网络。<bookmark mark='b'/>前一天，物理学奖授予了约翰·霍普菲尔德和杰弗里·辛顿，表彰第20部分讲过的那些网络。<bookmark mark='c'/>测定一个蛋白质的形状，实验室可能要花好几年；AlphaFold几分钟就能预测出一个。

8def9a6015bd.en: Here is the idea this part is built on. Five charged particles, a toy molecule: turn it, and its energy can't change. <bookmark mark='a'/> We trained networks on three thousand such molecules to predict the energy, then turned this one a full circle. <bookmark mark='b'/> A plain network doesn't know that turning is harmless: its answer swings over 1.73 units. <bookmark mark='c'/> Shown turned copies in training, over 0.08. <bookmark mark='d'/> A network built on the distances between particles can't see the turn: its answer changes by less than a millionth of a unit, rounding error, and sits 0.00 from the true energy.
8def9a6015bd.zh: 这就是本部分立足的想法。五个带电粒子，一个玩具分子：把它转一转，它的能量不可能变。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们用三千个这样的分子训练网络去预测能量，然后把这一个转了整整一圈。<bookmark mark='b'/>普通网络不知道转动无害：它的答案摆动了1.73个单位。<bookmark mark='c'/>训练时给它看转过的副本，摆动0.08。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个建立在粒子间距离之上的网络看不见这次转动：它的答案只变了不到百万分之一个单位，只是舍入误差，离真实能量0.00。

4b3d5a6f9f85.en: That is the question of this part: what does a network gain by knowing the symmetries of its problem, and what has that done for science, <bookmark mark='a'/> in proteins, <bookmark mark='b'/> weather, <bookmark mark='c'/> materials <bookmark mark='d'/> and mathematics? Every experiment is computed here; every number about the big systems is quoted from their papers.
4b3d5a6f9f85.zh: 这就是本部分的问题：一个网络知道了它所处理问题的对称性，能得到什么？这又为科学做了什么，<bookmark mark='a'/>在蛋白质、<bookmark mark='b'/>天气、<bookmark mark='c'/>材料<bookmark mark='d'/>和数学里？每个实验都在这里计算；关于大系统的每个数字都引自它们的论文。

0bfe60010bc2.en: This is Part 25 of AI, Built, the last of its fourth act. <bookmark mark='a'/> In it: symmetry, and what it means for a function to respect it; <bookmark mark='o2'/> graphs, message passing, and its limits; <bookmark mark='o3'/> networks that turn with the molecule; <bookmark mark='o4'/> proteins, from the folding problem to AlphaFold and design; <bookmark mark='o5'/> fields: weather, neural operators, and materials; <bookmark mark='o6'/> and mathematics, from olympiad geometry to checked proofs and discovery by search.
0bfe60010bc2.zh: 这是《人工智能，从零搭建》的第25部分，也是第四幕的最后一部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>内容包括：对称性，以及一个函数尊重对称性是什么意思；<bookmark mark='o2'/>图、消息传递，以及它的极限；<bookmark mark='o3'/>随分子一起转动的网络；<bookmark mark='o4'/>蛋白质，从折叠问题到AlphaFold和蛋白质设计；<bookmark mark='o5'/>场：天气、神经算子，以及材料；<bookmark mark='o6'/>还有数学，从奥赛几何到经过检查的证明，再到靠搜索做出的发现。

79554faf59d2.en: Chapter one. How we got here.
79554faf59d2.zh: 第1章。我们是怎么走到这里的。

0cefd6fe11ab.en: This part's story has three threads, starting far apart. <bookmark mark='m0'/> The first computer weather forecast, 1950. <bookmark mark='m1'/> The first protein seen in three dimensions, 1958, and in 1961 Christian Anfinsen's discovery that the sequence decides the shape. <bookmark mark='m2'/> In 1968, a test of whether two graphs are the same, which turns out to measure what graph networks can see. <bookmark mark='m3'/> The Protein Data Bank, 1971; <bookmark mark='m4'/> the first forecast of Europe's weather centre, 1979; <bookmark mark='m5'/> convolutions, with the symmetry of images built in, 1989; <bookmark mark='m6'/> CASP's blind contests, 1994; <bookmark mark='m7'/> the first neural networks on graphs, 2005.
0cefd6fe11ab.zh: 本部分的故事有三条线索，起点相隔很远。<bookmark mark='m0'/>第一次计算机天气预报，1950年。<bookmark mark='m1'/>第一个在三维中看到的蛋白质，1958年；1961年，克里斯蒂安·安芬森发现序列决定形状。<bookmark mark='m2'/>1968年，一个判断两个图是否相同的测试，后来发现它衡量的正是图网络能看见什么。<bookmark mark='m3'/>蛋白质数据库，1971年；<bookmark mark='m4'/>欧洲天气中心的第一次预报，1979年；<bookmark mark='m5'/>内置了图像对称性的卷积，1989年；<bookmark mark='m6'/>CASP的盲测比赛，1994年；<bookmark mark='m7'/>最早的图神经网络，2005年。

8db364f41ab9.en: Then, within a decade, the threads met. <bookmark mark='d0'/> 2017: message passing, and networks for sets and molecules. <bookmark mark='d1'/> 2018: the first AlphaFold wins CASP; in 2020 AlphaFold 2 comes close to experiment. <bookmark mark='d2'/> 2021: networks that turn with a molecule, and networks that learn solutions of equations. <bookmark mark='d3'/> 2022: predicted structures for over two hundred million proteins. <bookmark mark='d4'/> 2023: a graph network out-forecasts the best weather model on most measures, and another proposes millions of new crystals. <bookmark mark='d5'/> 2024: the Nobel Prize, AlphaFold 3, machines solving olympiad problems; <bookmark mark='d6'/> 2025: AI forecasts in daily operation, new mathematics from evolutionary search; <bookmark mark='d7'/> 2026: open Erdős problems resolved by AI.
8db364f41ab9.zh: 然后，在十年之内，这些线索交汇了。<bookmark mark='d0'/>2017年：消息传递，以及处理集合和分子的网络。<bookmark mark='d1'/>2018年：第一代AlphaFold赢得CASP；2020年，AlphaFold 2接近实验水平。<bookmark mark='d2'/>2021年：随分子一起转的网络，以及学会方程解的网络。<bookmark mark='d3'/>2022年：两亿多个蛋白质的预测结构。<bookmark mark='d4'/>2023年：一个图网络在大多数指标上预报得比世界上最好的天气模型还准，另一个提出了数百万种新晶体。<bookmark mark='d5'/>2024年：诺贝尔奖，AlphaFold 3，机器解出奥赛题；<bookmark mark='d6'/>2025年：AI预报投入日常业务，进化搜索带来新的数学；<bookmark mark='d7'/>2026年：埃尔德什的未解问题被AI解决。

0182affa952f.en: What ties these together is one recipe. <bookmark mark='a'/> Ask what about your data doesn't matter. For an image, where the object sits: so convolutions. <bookmark mark='b'/> For a set of points, their order. <bookmark mark='c'/> For a graph, how its nodes are numbered. <bookmark mark='d'/> For a molecule, how it is turned or moved. <bookmark mark='e'/> A protein has all of these. <bookmark mark='f'/> A weather field lives on a sphere, whatever the grid. <bookmark mark='g'/> Language has little symmetry, so the transformer learns its structure from data. <bookmark mark='h'/> Bronstein, Bruna, Cohen and Veličković called this geometric deep learning. A symmetry enters a model three ways: transformed copies, a standard pose, or layers that respect it; this part is mostly about the third.
0182affa952f.zh: 把这些串起来的是同一个配方。<bookmark mark='a'/>问问你的数据有什么是无关紧要的。对图像来说，是物体在哪里：于是有了卷积。<bookmark mark='b'/>对一组点来说，是它们的顺序。<bookmark mark='c'/>对一个图来说，是节点怎么编号。<bookmark mark='d'/>对一个分子来说，是它怎么转、怎么移。<bookmark mark='e'/>蛋白质这些全都有。<bookmark mark='f'/>天气场位于球面上，与网格无关。<bookmark mark='g'/>语言几乎没有对称性，所以Transformer要从数据中学习结构。<bookmark mark='h'/>布朗斯坦、布鲁纳、科恩和韦利奇科维奇把这称为几何深度学习。对称性进入模型有三条路：转换过的副本，一个标准姿态，或者尊重它的网络层；本部分主要讲第三条。

6f444cb199e7.en: A symmetry is a transformation that leaves what matters unchanged. Turn a square by ninety degrees: the same square. <bookmark mark='a'/> Turn it four times and you are back. <bookmark mark='b'/> A problem's transformations form a group: you can compose them, one does nothing, and each can be undone. <bookmark mark='c'/> The square has four turns; the orderings of sixteen points, sixteen factorial, about 21 trillion. <bookmark mark='d'/> Turns of space form a continuous group, SO(3); an image has its shifts.
6f444cb199e7.zh: 对称是一种让要紧的东西保持不变的变换。把正方形转九十度：还是同一个正方形。<bookmark mark='a'/>转四次就回到原处。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个问题的变换构成一个群：可以复合，有一个什么都不做的变换，而且每个变换都能撤销。<bookmark mark='c'/>正方形有四种转动；十六个点的排列有十六的阶乘种，大约21万亿。<bookmark mark='d'/>空间的转动构成一个连续群，SO(3)；图像则有它的平移。

d4068f64002c.en: Now a function of the data, f: here, where each of our five particles will be one time unit later. <bookmark mark='a'/> Turn the input, then apply f, <bookmark mark='b'/> or apply f, then turn the output. <bookmark mark='c'/> If the two paths always agree, f is equivariant. <bookmark mark='d'/> If the output doesn't change at all, f is invariant, like an energy or an image's label. <bookmark mark='e'/> Inner layers need equivariance, so that the input's orientation isn't thrown away; a final answer often needs invariance.
d4068f64002c.zh: 现在来看数据的一个函数f：这里是我们五个粒子各自在一个时间单位之后的位置。<bookmark mark='a'/>先转输入，再用f，<bookmark mark='b'/>或者先用f，再转输出。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果两条路总是一致，f就是等变的。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果输出根本不变，f就是不变的，比如能量，或者图像的标签。<bookmark mark='e'/>中间层需要等变，这样输入的朝向才不会被扔掉；最终答案则常常需要不变。

7f11f23c0b59.en: Any function can be made equivariant by averaging it over the group: for each g, transform the input, apply f, undo g. <bookmark mark='a'/> Feed the average a turned input, h of x. <bookmark mark='b'/> Rename g times h as g prime: it runs through the group as g does, so the sum is the same. <bookmark mark='c'/> The inverse of a product reverses its order, <bookmark mark='d'/> and h comes out of the sum: the average is equivariant, whatever f was. <bookmark mark='e'/> The price: one evaluation per group element, sixteen factorial for sixteen points, infinitely many for turns of space. <bookmark mark='f'/> Augmentation is the cheap version: one random transformation per example, hoping the network learns the rest.
7f11f23c0b59.zh: 任何函数都能通过在群上取平均变成等变的：对每个g，先变换输入，再用f，再撤销g。<bookmark mark='a'/>给这个平均输入一个转过的x，也就是h作用在x上。<bookmark mark='b'/>把g乘h改名为g′：g走遍整个群时，g′也走遍整个群，所以和不变。<bookmark mark='c'/>乘积的逆要倒过顺序，<bookmark mark='d'/>于是h从和里提了出来：无论f是什么，平均都是等变的。<bookmark mark='e'/>代价是：群里每个元素算一次，十六个点就是十六的阶乘次，空间转动则是无穷多次。<bookmark mark='f'/>数据增强是便宜的版本：每个样本随机变换一次，指望网络学会其余的。

8ca076b03b93.en: Here is the check on our five-particle system: four networks, the same data, the same number of steps. <bookmark mark='a'/> Pause and predict: which turns its answer exactly when the input is turned? <bookmark mark='b'/> The equivariant network, EGNN, built in chapter seven: its turned and shifted answers are off by about a ten-millionth of a unit, rounding error. <bookmark mark='c'/> A message-passing network on raw coordinates handles a reordering exactly, not a turn. <bookmark mark='d'/> The plain MLP gets neither; trained on turned copies, its turning error is 0.06, smaller than its own error, but not zero. <bookmark mark='e'/> Symmetry built into the layers holds exactly, on every input; learned from examples, only approximately, near the data.
8ca076b03b93.zh: 这是在我们五粒子系统上的检验：四个网络，同样的数据，同样的步数。<bookmark mark='a'/>停下来预测一下：输入转动时，哪个网络的答案会精确地跟着转？<bookmark mark='b'/>等变网络EGNN，第7章会搭建它：它转过、平移过的答案只差大约千万分之一个单位，是舍入误差。<bookmark mark='c'/>读原始坐标的消息传递网络能精确处理重新编号，处理不了转动。<bookmark mark='d'/>普通MLP两样都不行；用转过的副本训练后，它的转动误差是0.06，比它自己的预测误差小，但不是零。<bookmark mark='e'/>做进网络层的对称性在每个输入上都精确成立；从例子里学来的只是近似成立，而且只在数据附近。

65eff021244a.en: Sixteen points in the plane, from one of four shapes: a ring, a disc, a segment, or two blobs. Say which. <bookmark mark='a'/> A plain network needs a list, so we number the points and feed it thirty-two coordinates. <bookmark mark='b'/> But the numbering is arbitrary: renumber, and the picture is the same while the list is not. <bookmark mark='c'/> A plain network trained on eight thousand sets sees a new input: its belief that this is a ring goes from 100 to 100 percent. <bookmark mark='d'/> Deep Sets, built for sets, gives exactly the same answer, as it must.
65eff021244a.zh: 平面上的十六个点，来自四种形状之一：圆环、圆盘、线段，或者两团。说出是哪一种。<bookmark mark='a'/>普通网络需要一个列表，所以我们给这些点编号，喂给它三十二个坐标。<bookmark mark='b'/>但编号是任意的：重新编号，图还是那张图，列表却变了。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个用八千个集合训练过的普通网络看到一个新输入：它认为这是一个环的把握，从100%变成了100%。<bookmark mark='d'/>为集合而建的Deep Sets给出完全相同的答案，它也必须如此。

b3ad077eed49.en: The theorem behind Deep Sets, from Manzil Zaheer and colleagues in 2017: a function of sets ignores order exactly when it is a sum of one function phi over the elements, followed by a function rho. <bookmark mark='a'/> One direction is easy: a sum ignores order. <bookmark mark='b'/> For the other, number every possible element, and let phi of x be four to the minus its number. <bookmark mark='c'/> In base four, the sum has a one in place k exactly when element k is in the set: no carries, so different sets give different sums. <bookmark mark='d'/> So any function of the set is a function of the sum. <bookmark mark='e'/> For sets of real numbers, power sums play this role, by Newton's identities.
b3ad077eed49.zh: Deep Sets背后的定理，出自曼齐尔·扎希尔等人2017年的工作：一个集合函数与顺序无关，当且仅当它是先对各元素求同一个函数phi的和，再接一个函数rho。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个方向很容易：和与顺序无关。<bookmark mark='b'/>另一个方向：给每个可能的元素编号，令phi(x)等于四的负编号次方。<bookmark mark='c'/>用四进制写，元素k在集合里，和的第k位就恰好是1：没有进位，所以不同的集合给出不同的和。<bookmark mark='d'/>于是集合的任何函数都是这个和的函数。<bookmark mark='e'/>对于实数集合，由牛顿恒等式，幂和起到同样的作用。

535ee10a211f.en: As a network, this is simple. <bookmark mark='a'/> The same small network phi reads every point, <bookmark mark='b'/> the results are summed, <bookmark mark='c'/> and a second network rho reads the sum. <bookmark mark='d'/> phi's weights are shared by every point, as a convolution shares its weights across positions. <bookmark mark='e'/> PointNet, the same year, used a maximum instead of the sum. And a transformer without positions treats its tokens as a set: reorder the inputs, and the outputs reorder with them.
535ee10a211f.zh: 做成网络，这很简单。<bookmark mark='a'/>同一个小网络phi读每个点，<bookmark mark='b'/>结果加起来，<bookmark mark='c'/>第二个网络rho读这个和。<bookmark mark='d'/>phi的权重被所有点共享，就像卷积在各个位置共享权重。<bookmark mark='e'/>同一年的PointNet用最大值代替了求和。而一个没有位置编码的Transformer把它的词元当作一个集合：输入重新排序，输出也跟着重新排序。

aa57c0071e36.en: Before the full comparison, watch one training run of each, on 512 training sets, the held-out accuracy checked every two hundred steps. <bookmark mark='a'/> Deep Sets passes eighty percent after 200 steps and ends at 99 percent. <bookmark mark='b'/> The plain MLP never gets to eighty percent; it ends at 47 percent. <bookmark mark='c'/> The MLP shown reordered copies gets there too, but later, at step 1,600, and ends at 96.
aa57c0071e36.zh: 在完整比较之前，先看每种网络的一次训练，用512组训练集合，每两百步检查一次留出集上的准确率。<bookmark mark='a'/>Deep Sets在200步之后超过80%，最后达到99%。<bookmark mark='b'/>普通MLP始终没有达到80%，最后停在47%。<bookmark mark='c'/>看重新排序副本的MLP也做到了，但更晚，在第1600步，最后达到96%。

4c0f1af15d93.en: Now train them on 32 up to 8,192 sets, three seeds each, the same number of steps. <bookmark mark='a'/> With only 32 sets, Deep Sets is right 70 percent of the time. <bookmark mark='b'/> The plain MLP is at 27 percent, and it needs 8,192 sets to reach what Deep Sets did with 32. <bookmark mark='c'/> Reordered copies help a lot: 60 percent at 32 sets. The MLP with reordered copies needs 128 sets to match that. Even at the largest size Deep Sets stays ahead: Deep Sets 100 percent, the copies 96. <bookmark mark='d'/> But copies teach the symmetry only approximately: reorder the same test sets, and the plain MLP changes its answer on 61 percent of them, the one trained on copies on 11 percent, Deep Sets on none.
4c0f1af15d93.zh: 现在来训练，从32组集合到8192组，每种三个种子，步数相同。<bookmark mark='a'/>只用32组集合，Deep Sets就有70%的时候是对的。<bookmark mark='b'/>普通MLP是27%，它需要8192组集合，才能达到Deep Sets用32组时的水平。<bookmark mark='c'/>重新排序的副本帮助很大：32组集合时是60%。用重新排序副本训练的MLP，需要128组集合才能追上这个水平。即使在最大的规模上，Deep Sets仍然领先：Deep Sets是100%，副本是96%。<bookmark mark='d'/>但副本只能近似地教会对称性：把同样的测试集合重新排序，普通MLP在61%的集合上改了答案，用副本训练的那个在11%的集合上改了答案，Deep Sets一个也没改。

37b71146e924.en: So building the symmetry in did two things: it saved data, and it made the answer exactly order-free, on every input. Graphs are next: sets with connections.
37b71146e924.zh: 所以，把对称性做进去带来了两件事：节省了数据，并且让答案在每个输入上都严格与顺序无关。接下来是图：带连接的集合。

8f39810b5702.en: A graph is a set with connections: nodes, and edges between some pairs. Here is decalin, ten carbons and eleven bonds. <bookmark mark='a'/> A computer stores it as an adjacency matrix, with a one wherever two nodes are joined. <bookmark mark='b'/> Number the nodes differently and its rows and columns shuffle, though the molecule is the same. <bookmark mark='c'/> So a network on graphs must be equivariant to renumbering: permute the nodes, and its answers permute the same way. <bookmark mark='d'/> Graphs are everywhere: molecules, road maps, social networks, weather meshes, and proteins, residues joined when close in space.
8f39810b5702.zh: 图是带连接的集合：节点，以及某些节点对之间的边。这是十氢萘，十个碳原子，十一根键。<bookmark mark='a'/>计算机把它存成一个邻接矩阵，两个节点相连的地方就是1。<bookmark mark='b'/>换一种方式给节点编号，它的行和列就被打乱了，而分子还是同一个。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以图上的网络必须对重新编号等变：把节点重新排列，它的答案也同样重新排列。<bookmark mark='d'/>图无处不在：分子、道路图、社交网络、天气网格，还有蛋白质，空间上挨得近的残基相连。

3d3de08b8cc8.en: In 2017 Justin Gilmer and colleagues at Google put these networks into one form, message passing. Every node keeps a state, a vector h. <bookmark mark='a'/> In each layer every node sums messages from its neighbours, a learned function M of the two states and the edge, <bookmark mark='b'/> then updates its state from the old one and the sum. <bookmark mark='c'/> A readout sums the final states into an answer about the whole graph. <bookmark mark='d'/> Every step is a sum over neighbours, so the numbering can't matter. <bookmark mark='e'/> The graph convolutional network of Thomas Kipf and Max Welling is the simplest case: average the neighbours' states, normalized by degree, and apply one weight matrix.
3d3de08b8cc8.zh: 2017年，谷歌的贾斯汀·吉尔默等人把这些网络归入一个统一的形式：消息传递。每个节点保存一个状态，一个向量h。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一层，每个节点把来自邻居的消息加起来，消息是两个状态和这条边的一个学出来的函数M，<bookmark mark='b'/>然后由旧状态和这个和更新自己的状态。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个读出把最后的状态加起来，给出关于整个图的答案。<bookmark mark='d'/>每一步都是对邻居求和，所以编号无关紧要。<bookmark mark='e'/>托马斯·基普夫和马克斯·韦林的图卷积网络是最简单的情形：按度数归一化，平均邻居的状态，再乘一个权重矩阵。

100e90cfe05f.en: The idea is older than its name. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1997 Alessandro Sperduti and Antonina Starita trained networks on labelled graphs. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2005 Marco Gori and colleagues proposed the graph neural network, its node states updated from their neighbours until they settled. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2014 Joan Bruna and colleagues defined convolutions through the graph's spectrum. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 2015 David Duvenaud and colleagues learned fingerprints of molecules. <bookmark mark='e'/> Gilmer's network then predicted thirteen quantum properties of small molecules, eleven within chemical accuracy. <bookmark mark='f'/> And Peter Battaglia and colleagues argued that graphs are the general way to give a network relational structure.
100e90cfe05f.zh: 这个想法比它的名字更早。<bookmark mark='a'/>1997年，亚历山德罗·斯佩尔杜蒂和安东尼娜·斯塔里塔在带标签的图上训练网络。<bookmark mark='b'/>2005年，马尔科·戈里等人提出了图神经网络，节点状态由邻居反复更新，直到稳定。<bookmark mark='c'/>2014年，琼·布鲁纳等人通过图的谱来定义卷积。<bookmark mark='d'/>2015年，大卫·杜维诺等人学会了分子的指纹。<bookmark mark='e'/>后来，吉尔默的网络预测了小分子的十三种量子性质，其中十一种达到化学精度。<bookmark mark='f'/>而彼得·巴塔利亚等人论证说，图是让网络具备关系结构的通用方式。

12be89b7cbec.en: Let's train one. Three hundred people in three communities, friendships mostly within: 89 percent of the edges, about 6 per person. Each carries only a weak, noisy hint of their community, and only 60 are labelled. <bookmark mark='a'/> A two-layer graph convolutional network learns from those labels and the graph: watch its guesses for everyone else. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two layers see two hops. <bookmark mark='c'/> An MLP that sees only each person's hint gets 46 percent right; the graph network 89 percent, over three seeds. Passing messages lifts it well above the hints alone.
12be89b7cbec.zh: 我们来训练一个。三百个人，分在三个社群里，友谊大多在社群内部：89%的边在社群内，平均每人大约6条。每个人只带着关于自己社群的一点微弱、嘈杂的线索，而且只有60个人有标签。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个两层的图卷积网络从这些标签和图中学习：看它对其他所有人的猜测。<bookmark mark='b'/>两层能看到两跳。<bookmark mark='c'/>只看每个人自己线索的MLP猜对46%；图网络猜对89%，三个种子的结果。传递消息让结果远远超过只看线索的水平。

f4a7a378e052.en: That is message passing: a learned sum over neighbours, repeated, so that after L layers each node has heard from everything within L hops. What can such a network tell apart?
f4a7a378e052.zh: 这就是消息传递：对邻居学出来的求和，一遍遍重复，于是L层之后，每个节点都听到了L跳以内的一切。这样的网络能分辨什么？

22ef87d71c0e.en: Chapter five. What message passing can't see.
22ef87d71c0e.zh: 第5章。消息传递看不见的东西。

4a36e7aca9b8.en: In 1968 Boris Weisfeiler and Andrei Leman described colour refinement, the standard first test of whether two graphs are the same up to numbering. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every node starts with one colour. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each round, a node's new colour names its old colour and its neighbours' colours: here the carbons with three neighbours split off. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then their neighbours, until nothing changes. Different colour counts mean different graphs. <bookmark mark='d'/> Decalin and bicyclopentyl, 3 rounds: At every round the two molecules have exactly the same colours in the same numbers, so the test says they might be the same graph. Yet one is two six-rings sharing an edge, the other two five-rings joined by a bond.
4a36e7aca9b8.zh: 1968年，鲍里斯·魏斯费勒和安德烈·莱曼描述了颜色细化，这是判断两个图在编号之外是否相同的标准初步测试。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个节点一开始都是同一种颜色。<bookmark mark='b'/>每一轮，节点的新颜色由它的旧颜色和邻居的颜色命名：这里，有三个邻居的碳原子分了出来。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后是它们的邻居，直到不再变化。颜色计数不同，图就不同。<bookmark mark='d'/>十氢萘和联环戊烷，3轮：每一轮，两个分子的颜色种类和数量都完全相同，所以检验说它们可能是同一个图。可一个是共用一条边的两个六元环，另一个是由一根键连起来的两个五元环。

94aea16a703a.en: And no message-passing network can do better. Keyulu Xu and colleagues, and Christopher Morris and colleagues, proved in 2019: if colour refinement can't separate two nodes after t rounds, no message-passing network separates them after t layers. <bookmark mark='a'/> By induction: at the start, everything is equal. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two nodes with the same colour next round had the same colour and the same multiset of neighbours' colours; <bookmark mark='c'/> by hypothesis, then, the same state and the same multiset of neighbours' states, <bookmark mark='d'/> from which a layer computes identical new states. <bookmark mark='e'/> And the bound is reached: a sum followed by an MLP, the graph isomorphism network, separates everything colour refinement does.
94aea16a703a.zh: 而且没有哪个消息传递网络能做得更好。Keyulu Xu等人，以及克里斯托弗·莫里斯等人，在2019年证明：如果颜色细化在t轮之后分不开两个节点，那么没有消息传递网络能在t层之后分开它们。<bookmark mark='a'/>用归纳法：一开始，一切都相同。<bookmark mark='b'/>下一轮颜色相同的两个节点，原来颜色相同，邻居颜色的多重集也相同；<bookmark mark='c'/>于是按归纳假设，状态相同，邻居状态的多重集也相同，<bookmark mark='d'/>一层网络从这些算出的新状态也就相同。<bookmark mark='e'/>而且这个上界能达到：求和之后接一个MLP，也就是图同构网络，能分开颜色细化能分开的一切。

8d9eab3fc90e.en: Why a sum? Aggregation must not lose information about the multiset of neighbours. <bookmark mark='a'/> Neighbours a, a, b, b and neighbours a, b have the same mean and the same maximum; only the sum differs. <bookmark mark='b'/> Computed: give every node of a random graph the same features, and ask a one-layer network for each node's degree. A sum gets within 0.00. <bookmark mark='c'/> A mean or a maximum, 1.46 and 1.46, hardly better than the spread of the degrees, 1.53: to them every node with a neighbour looks alike.
8d9eab3fc90e.zh: 为什么是求和？聚合不能丢掉关于邻居多重集的信息。<bookmark mark='a'/>邻居a、a、b、b和邻居a、b的平均值相同，最大值也相同；只有和不同。<bookmark mark='b'/>计算一下：给一个随机图的每个节点同样的特征，让一个单层网络说出每个节点的度。用求和，误差在0.00以内。<bookmark mark='c'/>用平均或最大值，分别是1.46和1.46，几乎不比度数的离散程度1.53好：在它们看来，每个有邻居的节点都一样。

3eaa8f466f5c.en: Now make a network fail on purpose. Graphs of 15 nodes that are unions of cycles: is there a triangle? <bookmark mark='a'/> To colour refinement they are all identical: every node has two neighbours, whose neighbours have two neighbours, forever. So every message-passing network must answer the same for all of them. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every graph gets exactly the same output, to the last digit, so GIN can do no better than always answering yes: 63.8 percent, the base rate. <bookmark mark='c'/> Giving every node a few random numbers breaks the symmetry in principle, but in our budget GIN never learned to use them: it stayed at the base rate in all three seeds. <bookmark mark='d'/> A network whose features live on pairs of nodes, updating each pair through every third node, sees triangles directly: 100.0 percent or better, in every seed, and its training curve leaves the base rate within a few hundred steps. Remember that construction: it is the heart of AlphaFold.
3eaa8f466f5c.zh: 现在故意让一个网络失败。15个节点、由若干个环组成的图：里面有没有三角形？<bookmark mark='a'/>在颜色细化看来，它们全都一样：每个节点都有两个邻居，邻居又各有两个邻居，一直如此。所以任何消息传递网络对它们都必须给出同一个答案。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个图得到的输出完全相同，一位都不差，所以GIN最多只能总是回答有：63.8%，也就是基准比例。<bookmark mark='c'/>给每个节点几个随机数，原则上能打破对称，但在我们的预算内，GIN始终没学会利用它们：三个种子全都停在基准比例。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个把特征放在节点对上、通过每个第三个节点更新每一对的网络，能直接看见三角形：每个种子都达到100.0%或更高，而且它的训练曲线在几百步之内就离开了基准比例。记住这个构造：它是AlphaFold的核心。

fe7e09bf7fbb.en: How bad is it in practice? On random graphs, hardly at all: colour refinement separated 300 of 300 different pairs. <bookmark mark='a'/> On graphs where every node has three neighbours, 0 of 100. <bookmark mark='b'/> The fixes add what a neighbour sum can't build: colouring tuples of nodes, at a cost growing as n to the k; counting triangles and other patterns; positions; or attention over every pair. <bookmark mark='c'/> Graph isomorphism itself is not known to be easy or hard; László Babai showed in 2016 that quasi-polynomial time suffices.
fe7e09bf7fbb.zh: 实际中有多糟？在随机图上，几乎不成问题：颜色细化分开了300对不同图中的300对。<bookmark mark='a'/>在每个节点都有三个邻居的图上，100对中只分开了0对。<bookmark mark='b'/>补救办法是加入邻居求和构造不出来的东西：给节点的元组上色，代价按n的k次方增长；数三角形和其他小图案；位置；或者覆盖每一对的注意力。<bookmark mark='c'/>图同构本身是容易还是困难，至今未知；拉斯洛·鲍鲍伊在2016年证明了拟多项式时间就够了。

b8a3c2b21c39.en: Graph networks are usually shallow, two to four layers; image networks run past a hundred. One reason: strip a graph convolution of its weights and it is an average over neighbours, applied again and again. <bookmark mark='a'/> The averaging matrix is symmetric, with orthonormal eigenvectors and eigenvalues at most one. <bookmark mark='b'/> Applying it k times raises each eigenvalue to the k. <bookmark mark='c'/> Every term but the first dies away; the first is one pattern on every node, scaled by the square root of its degree. <bookmark mark='d'/> The rate is the second eigenvalue to the k. <bookmark mark='e'/> Every node ends with the same features: over-smoothing, named by Qimai Li and colleagues in 2018.
b8a3c2b21c39.zh: 图网络通常很浅，两到四层；图像网络则超过一百层。原因之一：把图卷积的权重去掉，它就是一个对邻居的平均，一遍又一遍地做。<bookmark mark='a'/>平均矩阵是对称的，有正交归一的特征向量，特征值都不超过1。<bookmark mark='b'/>用它k次，就把每个特征值变成k次方。<bookmark mark='c'/>除第一项以外的每一项都衰减掉了；第一项在每个节点上是同一个图样，按度数的平方根缩放。<bookmark mark='d'/>衰减速率是第二特征值的k次方。<bookmark mark='e'/>每个节点最后都有同样的特征：过平滑，由Qimai Li等人在2018年命名。

5a9da6eeae25.en: Here it is on our three-community graph: the Dirichlet energy, how much neighbours differ, after each round of averaging. <bookmark mark='a'/> It falls in a straight line on this log scale, 4 powers of ten in sixteen rounds, at the rate the second eigenvalue, 0.915, predicts. <bookmark mark='b'/> In pictures: the features start as noise; a few rounds separate the communities, which is why two layers help; many rounds collapse everything to a point.
5a9da6eeae25.zh: 这是在我们的三社群图上：狄利克雷能量，也就是邻居之间差多少，在每一轮平均之后的值。<bookmark mark='a'/>在这个对数坐标上它沿直线下降，十六轮下降了4个数量级，正是第二特征值0.915预言的速率。<bookmark mark='b'/>用图来看：特征一开始是噪声；几轮平均把社群分开，这就是两层网络有帮助的原因；很多轮之后，一切都坍缩成一个点。

a3f6103b528d.en: Now with weights and training: the same task at depths from two to sixty-four, three seeds each. <bookmark mark='a'/> The plain network does best with the fewest, 2 layers; from 8 layers on, the plain network is at chance, about one in three. <bookmark mark='b'/> The residual network, which adds each layer's output to its input, holds at 94 percent at 64 layers: the skip connection keeps each node's own information from being averaged away, the fix that made image networks deep in Part 9. <bookmark mark='c'/> Part of the collapse is also an optimization problem: gradients must pass back through all those averages.
a3f6103b528d.zh: 现在加上权重和训练：同一个任务，深度从二到六十四，每个深度三个种子。<bookmark mark='a'/>普通网络在the fewest, 2层时最好；从8层开始，普通网络就只有瞎猜的水平，大约三分之一。<bookmark mark='b'/>残差网络把每一层的输出加回到它的输入上，在64层时仍保持在94%：跳跃连接让每个节点自己的信息不被平均掉，正是第9部分里让图像网络变深的那个办法。<bookmark mark='c'/>坍缩的一部分也是优化问题：梯度必须穿过所有这些平均反传回来。

de42fe722201.en: A second problem appears when the answer depends on distant nodes. <bookmark mark='a'/> The nodes within L hops can grow exponentially, <bookmark mark='b'/> yet all their information must squeeze into one fixed-size vector. <bookmark mark='c'/> Uri Alon and Eran Yahav called this over-squashing, in 2021; Jake Topping and colleagues traced it to bottlenecks. <bookmark mark='d'/> Remedies: rewire the graph, add nodes that see everything, or attend to every node directly.
de42fe722201.zh: 当答案依赖远处的节点时，第二个问题就出现了。<bookmark mark='a'/>L跳以内的节点可以指数增长，<bookmark mark='b'/>可它们所有的信息都得挤进一个固定大小的向量。<bookmark mark='c'/>乌里·阿隆和埃兰·亚哈夫在2021年把这叫作过挤压；杰克·托平等人把它追溯到瓶颈。<bookmark mark='d'/>补救：重新连图，加入能看见一切的节点，或者直接对每个节点做注意力。

e6e286c7cd3a.en: Attention is the third idea. <bookmark mark='a'/> Instead of summing its neighbours equally, a node weighs them: in Petar Veličković's graph attention network of 2018, by a softmax of learned scores. <bookmark mark='b'/> GATv2, from Shaked Brody and colleagues, fixed a flaw: the original scores ranked neighbours the same way for every node. <bookmark mark='c'/> A transformer, from Part 13, is this on the complete graph; <bookmark mark='d'/> graph transformers add the graph back as encodings of where each node sits. <bookmark mark='e'/> And AlphaFold's core is attention over pairs of residues, biased by triangles: last chapter's pair network, grown up.
e6e286c7cd3a.zh: 注意力是第三个想法。<bookmark mark='a'/>节点不再平等地加总邻居，而是给它们加权：在彼得·韦利奇科维奇2018年的图注意力网络里，权重是学出来的分数的softmax。<bookmark mark='b'/>沙凯德·布罗迪等人的GATv2修正了一个缺陷：原来的分数对每个节点都按同样的方式给邻居排序。<bookmark mark='c'/>第13部分的Transformer，就是完全图上的这种网络；<bookmark mark='d'/>图Transformer再把图加回来，编码每个节点所处的位置。<bookmark mark='e'/>而AlphaFold的核心是残基对上的注意力，由三角形加偏置：上一章的节点对网络，长大了。

594202c74d80.en: So deep graph networks fight two forces: repeated averaging washes out the differences between nodes, and bottlenecks squash distant information. Skip connections and attention push back. Next: the symmetry of space itself.
594202c74d80.zh: 所以深层图网络要对抗两股力量：反复平均会抹掉节点之间的差别，而瓶颈会挤压远处的信息。跳跃连接和注意力能顶回去。接下来：空间本身的对称性。

aafac7f8d3a2.en: Chapter seven. Networks that turn with the molecule.
aafac7f8d3a2.zh: 第7章。随分子一起转动的网络。

7de8b221a0a4.en: For molecules the symmetry is the group of rigid motions of space, E of three: rotations, reflections, translations. <bookmark mark='a'/> A molecule's energy is invariant under all of them. <bookmark mark='b'/> Differentiate both sides in the positions: the chain rule brings out the transpose of R. <bookmark mark='c'/> Multiply by R, <bookmark mark='d'/> and since forces are minus the gradient, they turn with the molecule: equivariant. So an invariant model of the energy gives equivariant forces for free.
7de8b221a0a4.zh: 对分子来说，对称是空间刚体运动构成的群，E(3)：转动、反射、平移。<bookmark mark='a'/>分子的能量在所有这些变换下不变。<bookmark mark='b'/>两边对位置求导：链式法则带出了R的转置。<bookmark mark='c'/>乘以R，<bookmark mark='d'/>又因为力是能量梯度的负值，力就随分子一起转：等变。所以一个不变的能量模型，免费给出等变的力。

9eb23df8b931.en: How do you build that into a network? The simplest answer is the E(n)-equivariant graph network of Victor Garcia Satorras, Emiel Hoogeboom and Max Welling, 2021. Each atom has features h and a position x. <bookmark mark='a'/> A message between two atoms sees their features and squared distance, nothing else. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each atom moves along the differences of positions, weighted by learned scalars; <bookmark mark='c'/> its features update from the summed messages, and stay invariant. <bookmark mark='d'/> Turn and shift the input: the messages are unchanged, the differences turn by R, the shift cancels, so the new positions are the old ones turned and shifted. <bookmark mark='e'/> SchNet, in 2017, had used distances alone.
9eb23df8b931.zh: 怎样把它做进网络里？最简单的答案是维克多·加西亚·萨托拉斯、埃米尔·胡赫博姆和马克斯·韦林2021年的E(n)等变图网络。每个原子有特征h和位置x。<bookmark mark='a'/>两个原子之间的消息只看它们的特征和距离的平方，别的都不看。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个原子沿着位置差移动，由学出来的标量加权；<bookmark mark='c'/>它的特征由加总的消息更新，保持不变。<bookmark mark='d'/>把输入转一转、移一移：消息不变，位置差跟着R转，平移抵消，于是新位置就是旧位置转过、移过的样子。<bookmark mark='e'/>2017年的SchNet只用了距离。

05fb5f1b5b3a.en: EGNN carries scalars, which don't turn, and positions, which turn like vectors. Richer models carry more. <bookmark mark='a'/> Any function on the sphere can be written in spherical harmonics of degree zero, one, two and up. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here, computed, is what one rotation does to the nine harmonics up to degree two: it mixes them only within each degree, in blocks of one, three and five; off the blocks, zero to 14 decimal places. <bookmark mark='c'/> So a network can keep features of each degree, turn each with its own block, and combine them by the Clebsch–Gordan rules of quantum angular momentum: <bookmark mark='d'/> the design of tensor field networks, NequIP and MACE, among today's most accurate learned force fields.
05fb5f1b5b3a.zh: EGNN携带标量，它们不转；还有位置，它们像向量一样转。更丰富的模型携带更多。<bookmark mark='a'/>球面上的任何函数都能用零阶、一阶、二阶以及更高阶的球谐函数写出来。<bookmark mark='b'/>这里计算的是一次转动对阶数不超过二的九个球谐函数做了什么：它只在每一阶内部混合，分成一、三、五三个块；块外精确到小数点后14位都是零。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以网络可以保留每一阶的特征，用各自的块来转，再按量子角动量的克莱布什–戈尔丹规则把它们组合起来：<bookmark mark='d'/>这就是张量场网络、NequIP和MACE的设计，它们属于当今最精确的学习力场。

4f7c5e4e6fd0.en: Does it pay? Our five-body system again: predict where the particles are at time one. Four networks, the same three thousand steps, from a hundred training systems up to 3,000, three seeds each. <bookmark mark='a'/> The dashed line is the simplest guess: every particle keeps going straight. <bookmark mark='b'/> The plain MLP ends at 0.082, no better than that guess of 0.074; turned copies help the MLP: 0.074. <bookmark mark='c'/> Message passing on raw coordinates: 0.011. <bookmark mark='d'/> EGNN: 0.0061, 14 times smaller than the MLP's. Trained on 1,000 systems, EGNN already beats every other network trained on 3,000.
4f7c5e4e6fd0.zh: 值得吗？还是我们的五体系统：预测粒子在时刻一的位置。四个网络，同样三千步训练，训练系统从一百个到3000个，每种三个种子。<bookmark mark='a'/>虚线是最简单的猜测：每个粒子都沿直线走下去。<bookmark mark='b'/>普通MLP最后是0.082，不比那个0.074的猜测好；转过的副本对MLP有帮助：0.074。<bookmark mark='c'/>读原始坐标的消息传递网络：0.011。<bookmark mark='d'/>EGNN：0.0061，比MLP的小14倍。只用1000个系统训练，EGNN就已经胜过了用3000个系统训练的所有其他网络。

8fa48c105a28.en: Here is training itself, for the runs on 3,000 systems: one test system the networks never saw, its five particles, and where they really go by time one, the blue paths. <bookmark mark='a'/> The crosses are each network's predicted end points, at checkpoints through training. <bookmark mark='b'/> EGNN's crosses settle onto the circles; by the end its predicted positions are off by 0.38 on average. The MLP's end 1.40 away.
8fa48c105a28.zh: 这是训练本身，用3000个系统的那几次训练：一个网络从没见过的测试系统，它的五个粒子，以及它们到时刻1真正走到哪里，蓝色的轨迹。<bookmark mark='a'/>叉号是每个网络在训练各个检查点预测的终点。<bookmark mark='b'/>EGNN的叉号落到了圆圈上；最后它预测的位置平均偏差0.38。MLP的偏差是1.40。

52469950fb4b.en: That is the case for equivariance: no data is spent teaching the network that a turned molecule is the same molecule. Proteins are molecules too; the rest of this part takes these ideas into science, starting with the hardest molecule of all.
52469950fb4b.zh: 这就是支持等变性的理由：不用花任何数据去教网络，转过的分子还是同一个分子。蛋白质也是分子；本部分其余的内容把这些想法带进科学，从最难的分子讲起。

77383262a0a5.en: A protein is a chain of amino acids, of twenty kinds, written by a gene. <bookmark mark='a'/> In water it folds into a precise shape, and the shape decides what it does: cut a molecule, grip a virus, open a channel. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 1958 John Kendrew saw the first, myoglobin, by X-ray crystallography. <bookmark mark='c'/> The Protein Data Bank opened in 1971 with seven structures; <bookmark mark='d'/> today it holds more than a quarter of a million. <bookmark mark='e'/> But we know billions of sequences, and a structure can take years to measure. Hence the problem: read the shape from the sequence.
77383262a0a5.zh: 蛋白质是一条由氨基酸连成的链，氨基酸有二十种，由一个基因写出。<bookmark mark='a'/>在水里它折叠成一个精确的形状，而形状决定了它做什么：切断一个分子，抓住一个病毒，打开一个通道。<bookmark mark='b'/>1958年，约翰·肯德鲁用X射线晶体学看到了第一个，肌红蛋白。<bookmark mark='c'/>蛋白质数据库在1971年开张时有7个结构；<bookmark mark='d'/>今天它收录了超过25万个。<bookmark mark='e'/>可我们知道几十亿条序列，而测定一个结构可能要好几年。于是就有了这个问题：从序列读出形状。

d00a0242ea29.en: Two facts frame the problem. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1961 Christian Anfinsen unfolded the enzyme ribonuclease with urea; washed out, it refolded by itself and worked again: the sequence holds the shape. <bookmark mark='b'/> But in 1969 Cyrus Levinthal pointed out that a chain can't find its shape by trying them all. <bookmark mark='c'/> Give each joint of a 100-residue chain three choices: about ten to the 47 shapes. <bookmark mark='d'/> At ten trillion a second, that is ten to the 26 years; the universe is ten to the ten years old. <bookmark mark='e'/> Yet proteins fold in microseconds to seconds. Nature doesn't search blindly, and neither should a computer.
d00a0242ea29.zh: 有两个事实给这个问题定了框架。<bookmark mark='a'/>1961年，克里斯蒂安·安芬森用尿素让核糖核酸酶解开折叠；洗掉尿素后，它自己折了回去，重新起作用：序列里就装着形状。<bookmark mark='b'/>但1969年，赛勒斯·列文索尔指出，一条链不可能靠逐个尝试来找到形状。<bookmark mark='c'/>给一条100个残基的链的每个关节三种选择：大约是十的47次方种形状。<bookmark mark='d'/>每秒试十万亿个，也要十的26次方年；宇宙的年龄是十的十次方年。<bookmark mark='e'/>可蛋白质在几微秒到几秒内就折叠好了。自然不会盲目搜索，计算机也不该。

25de9e701267.en: In 1994 John Moult and Krzysztof Fidelis turned the problem into a contest, CASP: every two years, predict structures measured but not yet published. <bookmark mark='a'/> Predictions are scored by GDT, roughly the percentage of residues within a few ångströms of their true place. <bookmark mark='b'/> Progress was slow for two decades; then evolution offered a clue. <bookmark mark='c'/> Line up the same protein from many species: when two positions touch, a mutation at one is often compensated at the other, so their columns change together; from around 2011, statistics could read contacts from them. <bookmark mark='d'/> At CASP13, in 2018, DeepMind's first AlphaFold predicted a histogram of distances for every residue pair, then folded a chain by gradient descent to match: high accuracy on 24 of the 43 hardest domains, against 14 for the next best.
25de9e701267.zh: 1994年，约翰·莫尔特和克日什托夫·菲德利斯把这个问题变成了一场比赛，CASP：每两年一次，预测那些已经测定、但尚未发表的结构。<bookmark mark='a'/>预测用GDT打分，大致是落在真实位置几埃以内的残基所占的百分比。<bookmark mark='b'/>二十年里进展很慢；然后，进化给出了线索。<bookmark mark='c'/>把许多物种的同一种蛋白质对齐：两个位置相互接触时，一处的突变常常由另一处来补偿，所以这两列一起变化；大约从2011年起，统计方法就能从中读出接触。<bookmark mark='d'/>2018年的CASP13上，DeepMind的第一代AlphaFold为每一对残基预测距离的直方图，再用梯度下降把链折成与之相符：在43个最难的结构域中，有24个达到高精度，第二名是14个。

6ce07d8f50bd.en: Why distances? Because a full table of distances fixes a shape. Here are all the distances between our bundle's fifty-two atoms. <bookmark mark='a'/> Square them and centre them, <bookmark mark='b'/> and you get the dot products of the atoms' positions, since a squared distance is two squared lengths minus twice a dot product. <bookmark mark='c'/> Its eigenvectors give the coordinates back: classical multidimensional scaling, 1952. Three eigenvalues are nonzero, one per dimension, <bookmark mark='d'/> and the rebuilt chain matches to rounding error. <bookmark mark='e'/> But only up to a mirror image, which has the same distances; and proteins are not mirror-symmetric: their helices are right-handed.
6ce07d8f50bd.zh: 为什么是距离？因为一张完整的距离表就确定了一个形状。这是我们螺旋束五十二个原子之间的所有距离。<bookmark mark='a'/>把它们平方，再中心化，<bookmark mark='b'/>就得到原子位置之间的点积，因为距离的平方等于两个长度的平方和减去两倍点积。<bookmark mark='c'/>它的特征向量把坐标还原出来：经典多维尺度分析，1952年。只有三个特征值非零，每个维度一个，<bookmark mark='d'/>还原出的链与原来的一致，只差舍入误差。<bookmark mark='e'/>但只能确定到一个镜像，镜像的距离完全相同；而蛋白质不是镜像对称的：它们的螺旋是右手螺旋。

8c0df4d216e7.en: AlphaFold 1 predicted only distances, noisy, and only for pairs it was sure were close. So do the same with ours: keep the pairs under 15 ångströms, 50 percent of them, add 1 ångström of noise, <bookmark mark='a'/> and from a random tangle, move the atoms by gradient descent until their distances match. <bookmark mark='b'/> From 12 random starts, seven of the 12 land on the true fold, and five on its mirror image, which fits the distances just as well. <bookmark mark='c'/> Nothing a reflection leaves unchanged, distances included, can tell which. AlphaFold 2 needed a representation that knows left from right.
8c0df4d216e7.zh: AlphaFold 1只预测距离，带噪声，而且只针对它确信挨得近的残基对。我们也这样做：只保留15埃以内的残基对，占50%，加上1埃的噪声，<bookmark mark='a'/>然后从一团随机的乱线出发，用梯度下降移动原子，直到距离吻合。<bookmark mark='b'/>从12个随机起点出发，12次里有7次落在真实的折叠上，5次落在它的镜像上，而镜像和距离吻合得一样好。<bookmark mark='c'/>凡是在反射下不变的东西，包括距离，都分不清是哪个。AlphaFold 2需要一种分得清左右的表示。

4766fa68e2ec.en: Distances pin down a shape, but only up to its mirror image. Keep that in mind; AlphaFold 2's answer to it is one of its cleverest parts.
4766fa68e2ec.zh: 距离能确定一个形状，但只能精确到镜像。记住这一点；AlphaFold 2对此的回答，是它最巧妙的部分之一。

c5bb55c248a0.en: AlphaFold 2, which John Jumper and colleagues at DeepMind entered in CASP14 in 2020, works in two stages. <bookmark mark='a'/> It searches genetic databases for related sequences, lined up in a multiple sequence alignment, and for similar known structures. <bookmark mark='b'/> The Evoformer, forty-eight blocks deep, reasons about these; <bookmark mark='c'/> the structure module turns the result into atoms, with a confidence per residue. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then it all runs again on its own output. <bookmark mark='e'/> The Evoformer keeps a vector per residue of every aligned sequence, and one per pair of residues, heir to AlphaFold 1's distance histograms.
c5bb55c248a0.zh: AlphaFold 2是约翰·江珀等人在2020年代表DeepMind参加CASP14的系统，它分两个阶段工作。<bookmark mark='a'/>它在基因数据库里搜索相关序列，排成一个多序列比对，再找相似的已知结构。<bookmark mark='b'/>Evoformer有四十八个模块那么深，对这些信息进行推理；<bookmark mark='c'/>结构模块把结果变成原子，并给每个残基一个置信度。<bookmark mark='d'/>然后整个系统在自己的输出上再跑一遍。<bookmark mark='e'/>Evoformer为比对中每条序列的每个残基保留一个向量，为每一对残基保留一个向量，后者继承了AlphaFold 1的距离直方图。

e2c60a1b876d.en: Each Evoformer block passes information both ways between them. <bookmark mark='a'/> Along each sequence, the residues attend to one another, with the pair representation biasing the attention. <bookmark mark='b'/> Down each column, the same position attends across species. <bookmark mark='c'/> And back the other way, an outer product of two columns of the alignment, averaged over the sequences, updates the pair of those positions: co-evolution, learned.
e2c60a1b876d.zh: 每个Evoformer模块都在这两者之间双向传递信息。<bookmark mark='a'/>沿着每条序列，残基彼此做注意力，残基对的表示给这个注意力加上偏置。<bookmark mark='b'/>沿着每一列，同一个位置在不同物种之间做注意力。<bookmark mark='c'/>反过来，比对里两列的外积，在所有序列上平均，更新这两个位置组成的那一对：学出来的共进化。

8bd8c6b322ec.en: The new idea is in how the pairs update each other. Think of the pair representation as a guess at every distance. <bookmark mark='a'/> The guesses can't be independent: for any third residue k, the distance from i to j is at most i to k plus k to j. <bookmark mark='b'/> So each pair i j is updated from the other two edges of every triangle it sits in: a gated sum over k of products of the pairs i k and j k, the 'outgoing' update; <bookmark mark='c'/> the same with the edges pointing in. <bookmark mark='d'/> In the matrix, entry i j collects rows i and j. <bookmark mark='e'/> Triangle attention does the same with attention weights. <bookmark mark='f'/> Chapter five's lesson: pairs updated through a third node see what single nodes cannot.
8bd8c6b322ec.zh: 新想法在于残基对怎样互相更新。把残基对的表示看成是对每个距离的猜测。<bookmark mark='a'/>这些猜测不可能互相独立：对任何第三个残基k，从i到j的距离最多是i到k加上k到j。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以每一对i、j都用它所在的每个三角形的另外两条边来更新：对k求和，把i k和j k这两对的乘积加起来，再加门控，这叫“外向”更新；<bookmark mark='c'/>指向内的边也同样处理。<bookmark mark='d'/>在矩阵里，元素i j收集第i行和第j行。<bookmark mark='e'/>三角注意力用注意力权重做同样的事。<bookmark mark='f'/>第5章的教训：通过第三个节点更新的节点对，能看见单个节点看不见的东西。

14f6b85d2b05.en: Does it work? A small test, computed here. Random protein-like chains of 20 residues; the model sees a quarter of the distances, with noise, and must fill in the rest, a stand-in for what an alignment tells AlphaFold. <bookmark mark='a'/> Two models of the same size and training: one updates each pair on its own, the other with triangle updates. <bookmark mark='b'/> Guessing each missing distance from the separation along the chain gives an error of 5.5 ångströms. Updating each pair on its own gets 6.2, no better: it never looks at the other pairs, and it knows the gap along the chain only up to eight. <bookmark mark='c'/> Triangle updates cut it to 1.4, 4.4 times smaller, and their guesses break the triangle inequality 9 times less often.
14f6b85d2b05.zh: 它管用吗？这里计算一个小测试。随机的、像蛋白质一样的链，20个残基；模型看到四分之一的距离，带噪声，要把其余的填出来，这代替了比对告诉AlphaFold的信息。<bookmark mark='a'/>两个同样大小、同样训练的模型：一个单独更新每一对，另一个用三角更新。<bookmark mark='b'/>只根据两个残基在链上隔多远来猜缺失的距离，误差是5.5埃。单独更新每一对得到6.2，并没有更好：它从不看别的残基对，而且它只知道链上八以内的间隔。<bookmark mark='c'/>Triangle updates cut it to 1.4，4.4 times smaller, and their guesses break the triangle inequality 9 times less often。

a7f25df626b4.en: Here is the training itself, replayed: both models' guesses for one held-out chain. <bookmark mark='a'/> At step zero both guess nothing in particular. <bookmark mark='b'/> Within a few hundred steps both learn the easy part, that neighbours along the chain are close in space: the dark band on the diagonal. <bookmark mark='c'/> The rest, which distant residues come back together, needs the other pairs; <bookmark mark='d'/> on the curve below, the triangle model passes the per-pair model's final error by step 250, and keeps going, to 1.5 ångströms against 6.2.
a7f25df626b4.zh: 这是训练过程本身的回放：两个模型对一条留出链的猜测。<bookmark mark='a'/>第0步，两个模型的猜测都没有什么特别的。<bookmark mark='b'/>几百步之内，两个都学会了容易的部分：链上相邻的残基在空间里也挨得近，也就是对角线上的那条深色带。<bookmark mark='c'/>剩下的部分，也就是链上相隔很远的残基又在哪里碰到一起，需要别的残基对；<bookmark mark='d'/>在下面的曲线上，三角模型在第250步就超过了逐对模型的最终误差，而且继续下降，到1.5埃，逐对模型是6.2埃。

9e6c7ae2feb6.en: And at CASP14, in 2020, it worked. <bookmark mark='a'/> AlphaFold 2's median score was 92.4 GDT over all targets, 87.0 on the hardest; around ninety is informally reckoned competitive with experiment. <bookmark mark='b'/> Its median backbone error was 0.96 ångström, against 2.8 for the next best; a carbon atom is about one and a half across. <bookmark mark='c'/> "We have been stuck on this one problem, how do proteins fold up, for nearly fifty years," said John Moult; CASP called it a solution, for single chains.
9e6c7ae2feb6.zh: 而在2020年的CASP14上，它成功了。<bookmark mark='a'/>AlphaFold 2在所有目标上的中位数得分是92.4 GDT，在最难的目标上是87.0；按非正式的看法，大约九十分就能和实验相比。<bookmark mark='b'/>它的主链误差中位数是0.96埃，第二名是2.8；一个碳原子的直径大约是1.5埃。<bookmark mark='c'/>“我们在这个问题上卡了将近五十年：蛋白质是怎么折叠起来的，”约翰·莫尔特说；CASP称之为一个解答，针对单条链。

fdd682e85e65.en: So the Evoformer's two ideas: let the alignment and the pairs inform each other, and keep the pairs consistent through triangles. Next: turn pairs into a structure without losing left from right.
fdd682e85e65.zh: 所以Evoformer的两个想法是：让比对和残基对互相提供信息，用三角形让残基对保持一致。下一步：把残基对变成一个结构，而且不弄丢左和右。

8ddd3d7631ab.en: Chapter ten. AlphaFold 2: frames, FAPE and recycling.

18a6d51e1f55.en: The structure module treats each residue as a rigid body: a triangle of three backbone atoms with its own frame, a rotation and a position. <bookmark mark='a'/> It starts with every frame at the origin, a residue gas, and moves them. <bookmark mark='b'/> Its invariant point attention places learned points in each residue's frame and scores pairs of residues by how close those points come. <bookmark mark='c'/> A rigid motion of the protein moves every point alike, so the attention can't change. <bookmark mark='d'/> Each layer nudges every frame by an update in that frame's own coordinates, so the updates turn with the protein: equivariance, built in.
18a6d51e1f55.zh: 结构模块把每个残基当作一个刚体：由三个主链原子组成的三角形，有它自己的坐标系，一个旋转加一个位置。<bookmark mark='a'/>它一开始把所有坐标系都放在原点，一团“残基气体”，然后移动它们。<bookmark mark='b'/>它的不变点注意力在每个残基的坐标系里放置一些学出来的点，按这些点靠得多近来给残基对打分。<bookmark mark='c'/>蛋白质的一次刚体运动让每个点都同样移动，所以注意力不会变。<bookmark mark='d'/>每一层用一个以该坐标系自身坐标表示的更新，轻轻推动每个坐标系，所以更新随蛋白质一起转动：等变性，做在了里面。

26eaad122a32.en: What should the network be trained to minimize? AlphaFold 2's answer is the frame-aligned point error, FAPE. <bookmark mark='a'/> Stand in residue i's frame and look at atom j. <bookmark mark='b'/> Do this for every atom from every frame, in prediction and truth, and average the differences, each capped at ten ångströms so outliers can't dominate. <bookmark mark='c'/> A rigid motion of the whole structure cancels: FAPE ignores where the protein sits and how it is turned. <bookmark mark='d'/> But frames are built from three atoms by a right-hand rule, and a mirror image is not a rigid motion, so FAPE sees it.
26eaad122a32.zh: 网络应该被训练去最小化什么？AlphaFold 2的答案是坐标系对齐点误差，FAPE。<bookmark mark='a'/>站在残基i的坐标系里看原子j。<bookmark mark='b'/>对每个原子、从每个坐标系都这样看，在预测里和真实结构里都看，把差别平均起来，每个差别截断在十埃，免得离群值主导结果。<bookmark mark='c'/>整个结构的刚体运动会抵消：FAPE不管蛋白质在哪里、朝哪个方向。<bookmark mark='d'/>但坐标系是用右手法则从三个原子构造的，而镜像不是刚体运动，所以FAPE能看出来。

f167ad83787b.en: Here is the difference, measured on our bundle and its reflection. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every distance is the same, so the distance error is 0.00. <bookmark mark='b'/> Yet FAPE is 0.79, worse than moving every atom a whole ångström at random, 0.59. <bookmark mark='c'/> And chapter eight's folds, which distances couldn't sort, separate cleanly: those on the true fold score 0.31, mirror images 0.80.
f167ad83787b.zh: 差别在这里，在我们的螺旋束和它的镜像上测量。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个距离都一样，所以距离误差是0.00。<bookmark mark='b'/>可FAPE是0.79，比把每个原子随机移动整整1埃还差，那样是0.59。<bookmark mark='c'/>而第8章那些光靠距离分不开的折叠，现在被干净地分开了：落在真实折叠上的得分0.31，镜像0.80。

fe0f2be09a3f.en: The last trick is recycling: run the network again on its own previous output, so that a rough first structure can sharpen the reading of the alignment. <bookmark mark='a'/> In training the number of passes is random and the gradient flows only through the last, so extra passes cost no memory. <bookmark mark='b'/> We added it to chapter nine's triangle model. In our toy the extra passes change little: from 1.87 to 1.83 ångströms at best, though even with four passes it doesn't beat the same network trained without recycling, 1.42: our toy feeds back only its guesses about pairs, with no structure in the loop, while in AlphaFold 2 recycling did help.
fe0f2be09a3f.zh: 最后一招是循环：把网络在它自己上一次的输出上再跑一遍，这样一个粗糙的初始结构就能让网络把比对读得更清楚。<bookmark mark='a'/>训练时，跑几遍是随机的，梯度只流过最后一遍，所以多跑几遍不多占内存。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们把它加到了第9章的三角模型上。在我们的玩具里，多跑几遍变化不大：从1.87埃到最好的1.83埃，不过即使跑四遍，它也没有胜过不用循环训练的同一个网络，1.42：我们的玩具送回去的只是它对残基对的猜测，回路里没有结构，而在AlphaFold 2里，循环确实有帮助。

681126dec6c3.en: In July 2021 DeepMind published AlphaFold 2 with its code; the same month David Baker's group published RoseTTAFold, built on the same insights. <bookmark mark='a'/> With EMBL's European Bioinformatics Institute, DeepMind then released predicted structures for over two hundred million proteins, <bookmark mark='b'/> each with the network's own residue-by-residue confidence, pLDDT. <bookmark mark='c'/> Two years later came the Nobel Prize. <bookmark mark='d'/> But AlphaFold 2 predicts one static shape per chain, and says little about how proteins bind DNA or hold a drug: the next step.
681126dec6c3.zh: 2021年7月，DeepMind发表了AlphaFold 2，并公开了代码；同一个月，大卫·贝克的团队发表了基于同样洞见的RoseTTAFold。<bookmark mark='a'/>随后，DeepMind和EMBL的欧洲生物信息研究所一起发布了两亿多个蛋白质的预测结构，<bookmark mark='b'/>每个都带着网络自己逐个残基给出的置信度，pLDDT。<bookmark mark='c'/>两年后，诺贝尔奖来了。<bookmark mark='d'/>但AlphaFold 2对每条链只预测一个静止的形状，对蛋白质怎样结合DNA、怎样夹住一个药物分子，说得很少：这是下一步。

d489be9018c8.en: So: residues as rigid frames, moved by attention that can't see how the protein is turned; a loss that ignores rigid motions but not reflections; and a network that reads its own answer and tries again.
d489be9018c8.zh: 所以：残基是刚性的坐标系，由看不见蛋白质怎么转的注意力来移动；一个不在乎刚体运动、却在乎反射的损失；还有一个会读自己的答案、再试一次的网络。

ff5851a3d731.en: Chapter eleven. AlphaFold 3: diffusion over atoms.

15819fbddbb5.en: In May 2024 Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs published AlphaFold 3. <bookmark mark='a'/> It takes almost anything in a cell's structures, protein chains, DNA and RNA, drug-like molecules, ions, modified residues, and predicts how they sit together. <bookmark mark='b'/> The alignment gets just four blocks; <bookmark mark='c'/> the trunk is the Pairformer, the Evoformer's pair stack, forty-eight blocks, triangle updates intact. <bookmark mark='d'/> The big change is the end: the structure module, frames and all, is replaced by a diffusion model that writes every atom's coordinates directly.
15819fbddbb5.zh: 2024年5月，谷歌DeepMind和Isomorphic Labs发表了AlphaFold 3。<bookmark mark='a'/>细胞结构里的几乎任何东西它都能处理，蛋白质链、DNA和RNA、类药分子、离子、修饰过的残基，并预测它们怎样待在一起。<bookmark mark='b'/>比对只经过四个模块；<bookmark mark='c'/>主干是Pairformer，也就是Evoformer的残基对部分，四十八个模块，三角更新原样保留。<bookmark mark='d'/>大的改变在最后：结构模块连同它的坐标系，被一个扩散模型取代，它直接写出每个原子的坐标。

683a0a0b77e1.en: Diffusion is Part 21's idea, applied to atoms. <bookmark mark='a'/> Add noise to a structure's coordinates, at every level from a whisper to pure noise, and train a network to remove it; then start from noise and remove it step by step. Here is a small model of ours, from noise to a chain. <bookmark mark='b'/> And here is the surprise, after four chapters of building symmetry in: the AlphaFold 3 paper says its architecture needs no invariance or equivariance to rotations or translations. <bookmark mark='c'/> Every training structure is simply centred and turned at random: augmentation, chapter two's cheap route. <bookmark mark='d'/> Diffusion can also invent structure in floppy regions; training on AlphaFold-Multimer's predictions taught AlphaFold 3 to leave them loose.
683a0a0b77e1.zh: 扩散是第21部分的想法，用在了原子上。<bookmark mark='a'/>给一个结构的坐标加噪声，从轻微到纯噪声的每个水平都加，训练一个网络去除掉噪声；然后从噪声出发，一步一步除掉它。这是我们的一个小模型，从噪声变成一条链。<bookmark mark='b'/>惊奇之处来了，就在花了四章把对称性做进网络之后：AlphaFold 3的论文说，它的架构不需要对转动或平移的不变性或等变性。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个训练结构只是先中心化，再随机转动：数据增强，第2章那条便宜的路。<bookmark mark='d'/>扩散还可能在松软的区域编造出结构；用AlphaFold-Multimer的预测来训练，教会了AlphaFold 3让这些区域保持松散。

fa698b0403c9.en: So is equivariance worth it, for a generator? A toy test: four thousand compact chains of twelve atoms in the plane, bonds of length one. <bookmark mark='a'/> Two denoisers, trained equally long: one equivariant to rotations, like EGNN; a plain MLP shown every chain turned at random, as AlphaFold 3 is. <bookmark mark='b'/> Their samples. <bookmark mark='c'/> Bonds: the equivariant model's are off by 0.075 on average, the plain one's by 0.113. Clashes, two atoms on top of each other: 73.6 percent of chains against 45.1. Each wins on one count, and neither simply copies its training chains. <bookmark mark='d'/> At AlphaFold 3's scale, with the whole Protein Data Bank, DeepMind chose turned copies: data and compute standing in for built-in symmetry.
fa698b0403c9.zh: 那么，对生成模型来说，等变性值得吗？做一个玩具测试：平面上四千条紧凑的链，每条十二个原子，键长为1。<bookmark mark='a'/>两个去噪器，训练时间一样长：一个对转动等变，像EGNN；另一个是普通MLP，每条链都随机转过之后才给它看，就像AlphaFold 3那样。<bookmark mark='b'/>它们的样本。<bookmark mark='c'/>键长：等变模型平均偏差0.075，普通模型0.113。碰撞，也就是两个原子叠在一起：73.6%的链对45.1%。两者各赢一项，而且两者都没有只是照抄训练链。<bookmark mark='d'/>在AlphaFold 3的规模上，有整个蛋白质数据库，DeepMind选择了转过的副本：用数据和算力代替内置的对称性。

d4495798e767.en: On drug-like molecules bound to proteins, DeepMind reported AlphaFold 3 fifty percent more accurate than the best traditional methods. <bookmark mark='a'/> It came as a free server, and in November 2024 as code and weights for academics; <bookmark mark='b'/> open reproductions followed: Chai-1, Boltz-1, Protenix. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2025 Boltz-2 added a prediction of binding strength. <bookmark mark='d'/> And in February 2026 Isomorphic Labs reported a proprietary successor that, on its own benchmark of new antibody–antigen pairs, makes high-accuracy predictions 2.3 times as often as AlphaFold 3.
d4495798e767.zh: 对于结合在蛋白质上的类药分子，DeepMind报告说AlphaFold 3比最好的传统方法精确百分之五十。<bookmark mark='a'/>它先以免费服务器的形式提供，2024年11月又向学术界开放了代码和权重；<bookmark mark='b'/>开放的复现随之而来：Chai-1、Boltz-1、Protenix。<bookmark mark='c'/>2025年，Boltz-2加上了对结合强度的预测。<bookmark mark='d'/>2026年2月，Isomorphic Labs报告了一个专有的后继系统：在它自己的新抗体–抗原对基准上，做出高精度预测的比例是AlphaFold 3的2.3倍。

d3fa0e9e09a3.en: AlphaFold 3 kept the pair stack, handed the geometry to diffusion, and learned the symmetry from turned copies. Prediction also runs backwards: from a shape you want, to a protein that folds into it.
d3fa0e9e09a3.zh: AlphaFold 3保留了残基对的部分，把几何交给了扩散，从转过的副本里学会对称性。预测也可以倒过来：从你想要的形状，到一个能折成它的蛋白质。

64dbcf183854.en: Structure prediction goes from a sequence to a shape. <bookmark mark='a'/> Design goes the other way: from a shape you want, a binder for a virus or a scaffold for a catalyst, to a sequence that folds into it. <bookmark mark='b'/> This was David Baker's life's work, the other half of the 2024 Nobel. In 2003 his group designed Top7, a fold unseen in nature, with the Rosetta energy function, and it folded as designed. For two decades, though, most designs failed.
64dbcf183854.zh: 结构预测是从序列到形状。<bookmark mark='a'/>设计走的是反方向：从你想要的形状，比如一个能结合病毒的结合子或一个催化剂的支架，到一条能折成它的序列。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是大卫·贝克毕生的工作，也是2024年诺贝尔奖的另一半。2003年，他的团队用Rosetta能量函数设计出了Top7，一种自然界从未见过的折叠，它按设计折叠了。不过二十年来，大多数设计都失败了。

c2e5c48af1fa.en: Deep learning changed both halves of design, starting with the sequence. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2022 Justus Dauparas and colleagues in Baker's lab built ProteinMPNN: it reads a backbone as a graph, each residue joined to its nearest neighbours in space, <bookmark mark='b'/> passes messages built from distances, so the backbone's orientation can't matter, <bookmark mark='c'/> and writes the amino acids one at a time, in random order, each conditioned on those already written. <bookmark mark='d'/> On natural backbones it recovers 52.4 percent of the native amino acids, against 32.9 for Rosetta.
c2e5c48af1fa.zh: 深度学习改变了设计的两半，先从序列说起。<bookmark mark='a'/>2022年，贝克实验室的尤斯图斯·道帕拉斯等人做出了ProteinMPNN：它把主链读成一个图，每个残基与空间中离它最近的邻居相连，<bookmark mark='b'/>传递由距离构成的消息，所以主链朝哪个方向都无关紧要，<bookmark mark='c'/>然后按随机顺序一次写一个氨基酸，每个都以已经写好的那些为条件。<bookmark mark='d'/>在天然主链上，它能还原出52.4%的天然氨基酸，Rosetta是32.9%。

49b1af35b25e.en: Then the backbone. In 2023 Joseph Watson and colleagues published RFdiffusion. <bookmark mark='a'/> They fine-tuned the structure predictor RoseTTAFold to remove noise from residue frames, on positions and orientations, two hundred steps from noise to a backbone, optionally holding a motif, binding a target or obeying a symmetry. <bookmark mark='b'/> The pipeline: diffuse a backbone; let ProteinMPNN write eight sequences for it; <bookmark mark='c'/> keep those AlphaFold 2 folds back onto the design, within two ångströms and confidently; <bookmark mark='d'/> only then go to the lab. <bookmark mark='e'/> For binders, nineteen percent worked, about a hundred times the earlier rate; one influenza binder's measured structure sat 0.63 ångströms from its design.
49b1af35b25e.zh: 然后是主链。2023年，约瑟夫·沃森等人发表了RFdiffusion。<bookmark mark='a'/>他们微调结构预测器RoseTTAFold，让它去除残基坐标系上的噪声，位置和朝向上的噪声，从噪声到一条主链走两百步，还可以让它保持一个基序、结合一个靶标或者满足某种对称性。<bookmark mark='b'/>流程是：扩散出一条主链；让ProteinMPNN为它写八条序列；<bookmark mark='c'/>只保留AlphaFold 2能折回到设计上的那些，误差在两埃以内、而且有把握；<bookmark mark='d'/>然后才进实验室。<bookmark mark='e'/>对于结合子，百分之十九成功了，大约是早先成功率的一百倍；一个流感结合子测出来的结构，离它的设计只有0.63埃。

01eef569c728.en: Our toy denoiser from the last chapter shows the idea in miniature. Here is its training: the loss, and samples drawn from the same eight noise seeds at each checkpoint. <bookmark mark='a'/> At first, tangles; then chains with nearly the right bond lengths; then compact folds, though 74 percent of the final samples still have two atoms too close, which the training chains never do. <bookmark mark='b'/> Are they new? The median sample sits 0.49 from its nearest training chain, against 0.22 for real chains it never saw: farther than genuinely new chains are: not copies, but not quite the real thing either.
01eef569c728.zh: 上一章的玩具去噪器能把这个想法缩小了展示出来。这是它的训练：损失，以及在每个检查点用同样八个噪声种子抽出的样本。<bookmark mark='a'/>一开始是乱线；然后是键长差不多正确的链；然后是紧凑的折叠，不过最后的样本里仍有74%有两个原子挨得太近，而训练链从来不会这样。<bookmark mark='b'/>它们是新的吗？样本的中位数离最近的训练链0.49，而它从没见过的真实链是0.22：比真正的新链离得更远：不是照抄，但也还不完全像真的。

3e6e474491b1.en: Since then the field has moved fast. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2024 Google DeepMind's AlphaProteo designed binders for medical targets, <bookmark mark='b'/> BindCraft designed them by gradient descent through AlphaFold 2 itself, <bookmark mark='c'/> and EvolutionaryScale's ESM3, a language model over sequence, structure and function, wrote a fluorescent protein far from any natural one. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 2025 RFdiffusion3 designed atom by atom, <bookmark mark='e'/> and BoltzGen appeared as an open alternative. <bookmark mark='f'/> Tools this capable could be misused; in 2024 many researchers signed commitments on responsible biodesign, including screening DNA synthesis.
3e6e474491b1.zh: 从那以后，这个领域发展得很快。<bookmark mark='a'/>2024年，谷歌DeepMind的AlphaProteo为医学靶标设计了结合子，<bookmark mark='b'/>BindCraft通过在AlphaFold 2本身里做梯度下降来设计结合子，<bookmark mark='c'/>EvolutionaryScale的ESM3，一个覆盖序列、结构和功能的语言模型，写出了一个和任何天然蛋白都相差很远的荧光蛋白。<bookmark mark='d'/>2025年，RFdiffusion3逐个原子地做设计，<bookmark mark='e'/>BoltzGen也作为一个开放的选择出现了。<bookmark mark='f'/>这么强大的工具可能被滥用；2024年，许多研究者签署了负责任生物设计的承诺，包括对DNA合成进行筛查。

3371e7c1d9ce.en: Design, in one line: diffuse a backbone, write a sequence for it, check that the sequence folds back, and only then make it. Now from molecules to the whole planet.
3371e7c1d9ce.zh: 一句话说设计：扩散出一条主链，为它写一条序列，检查这条序列能不能折回去，然后才把它做出来。现在从分子走向整个星球。

4dd4095cfe9a.en: Chapter thirteen. Weather on a mesh.

f89eb8ee83ba.en: Weather forecasting became physics in 1904, when Vilhelm Bjerknes framed it as an initial-value problem: measure the atmosphere now, then step the equations of fluid flow forward. <bookmark mark='a'/> Lewis Fry Richardson tried it by hand in the First World War: six weeks of work for a six-hour forecast at two points, wrong by a hundred and forty-five hectopascals. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 1950 the first computer forecasts ran on ENIAC, about as fast as the weather itself. <bookmark mark='c'/> ECMWF, the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, first forecast in 1979; since then forecasts have gained about a day of skill per decade.
f89eb8ee83ba.zh: 1904年，天气预报变成了物理学：维尔赫姆·皮耶克尼斯把它表述成一个初值问题，测出此刻的大气，再把流体方程向前推进。<bookmark mark='a'/>刘易斯·弗赖·理查森在第一次世界大战期间试着用手算：花了六个星期，为两个点做出一次六小时预报，结果错了一百四十五百帕。<bookmark mark='b'/>1950年，最早的计算机预报在ENIAC上运行，算得和天气本身差不多快。<bookmark mark='c'/>欧洲中期天气预报中心，ECMWF，在1979年发布了第一次预报；此后，预报大约每十年多出一天的技巧。

5d7e0d44cf85.en: Machine learning came to this in the 2020s, trained on ERA5, ECMWF's reconstruction of global weather since 1940. In 2023 Remi Lam and colleagues at Google DeepMind published GraphCast. <bookmark mark='a'/> The atmosphere is stored on a latitude–longitude grid, a million points of two hundred and twenty-seven numbers each, crowded near the poles; GraphCast works on a mesh instead: <bookmark mark='b'/> an icosahedron refined six times, keeping every level's edges, so that a message crosses the planet in a few steps. Here is our small version, on a square. <bookmark mark='c'/> Encode onto the mesh, pass messages sixteen times, decode: the state six hours on, from the last two. <bookmark mark='d'/> It makes a ten-day forecast in under a minute, and beat ECMWF's flagship deterministic forecast on ninety percent of 1,380 targets.
5d7e0d44cf85.zh: 到了2020年代，机器学习来到了这里，用ERA5训练，那是ECMWF对1940年以来全球天气的重建。2023年，谷歌DeepMind的雷米·拉姆等人发表了GraphCast。<bookmark mark='a'/>大气存储在一个经纬度网格上，一百万个点，每个点二百二十七个数，在两极附近挤得很密；GraphCast改在一个网格网上工作：<bookmark mark='b'/>一个细分六次的正二十面体，保留每一层的边，于是一条消息几步就能穿过整个星球。这是我们的小版本，在一个正方形上。<bookmark mark='c'/>编码到网格网上，传递十六次消息，再解码：由最近的两个状态得到六小时之后的状态。<bookmark mark='d'/>它不到一分钟就能做出一次十天预报，并在1380个目标中的百分之九十上胜过了ECMWF旗舰的确定性预报。

88d65e4a253e.en: Ours is a toy atmosphere: a two-dimensional fluid on a square that wraps around, stirred by a fixed pattern and damped by friction, so that eddies form, drift, merge and die: chaotic, like the weather. <bookmark mark='a'/> A small encode–process–decode network on our mesh learns one step at a time from thirty-two simulated runs, then rolls forward on its own predictions. <bookmark mark='b'/> Top, the truth; bottom, our network, from the same start. They agree for a while, then drift apart.
88d65e4a253e.zh: 我们的是一个玩具大气：一个二维流体，在一个首尾相接的正方形上，被一个固定的图样搅动，又被摩擦减弱，于是涡旋生成、漂移、合并、消亡：混沌，就像天气。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个小的编码–处理–解码网络在我们的网格网上，从三十二次模拟中一步一步地学习，然后在自己的预测上往前推。<bookmark mark='b'/>上面是真实情况；下面是我们的网络，从同一个起点出发。它们一致一段时间，然后渐行渐远。

4f2922f980d1.en: Scored over eight new runs: the error, step by step. <bookmark mark='a'/> One step ahead its error is 0.35, against 0.59 for assuming nothing changes. <bookmark mark='b'/> It stays ahead of persistence for 15 steps, and after 15 steps it is worse than simply forecasting the average state, as every forecast of a chaotic system eventually is. GraphCast was trained on rollouts of up to twelve steps for exactly this reason, to learn from its own drifting predictions; ours rolled out two steps at the end of training. <bookmark mark='c'/> Over the first ten steps the long edges make no difference; they matter later: by step twenty the network with only the shortest edges is off by 3.7, against 2.7, in one training run of each.
4f2922f980d1.zh: 在八次新的模拟上打分：误差，一步一步看。<bookmark mark='a'/>提前一步，它的误差是0.35，而假设什么都不变的误差是0.59。<bookmark mark='b'/>在15步之内它都领先于持续性预报，而15步之后，它比直接预报平均状态还差，每个混沌系统的预报最终都会这样。GraphCast训练时最多展开十二步，正是为了这个原因，从自己逐渐偏离的预测里学习；我们的网络在训练的最后阶段展开两步。<bookmark mark='c'/>在前十步里，长边没有带来差别；它们的作用在后面：到第二十步，只用最短边的网络误差是3.7，而多尺度网格是2.7，这是每个网络各训练一次的结果。

02f5db7a3013.en: There is a deeper problem. Trained on squared error, a network predicts the average of what might happen, and far ahead the average of many weathers is a blur. <bookmark mark='a'/> Forecasters answer with ensembles, many runs from slightly different starts. In 2024 Google DeepMind's GenCast learned to sample the next state with diffusion; its ensembles beat ECMWF's on 97.2 percent of 1,320 targets. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then learned models went into daily service: ECMWF's AI Forecasting System in February 2025, its ensemble version that July, <bookmark mark='c'/> Google's WeatherNext 2 in November, and in December the first AI global models of America's NOAA.
02f5db7a3013.zh: 还有一个更深的问题。用平方误差训练，网络预测的是可能发生的情况的平均，而在很远的将来，许多种天气的平均是一片模糊。<bookmark mark='a'/>预报员用集合预报来应对：从略有不同的起点出发跑很多次。2024年，谷歌DeepMind的GenCast学会了用扩散来抽样下一个状态；它的集合预报在1320个目标中的97.2%上胜过了ECMWF的集合预报。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后，学出来的模型投入了日常业务：2025年2月是ECMWF的人工智能预报系统，那年7月是它的集合版本，<bookmark mark='c'/>11月是谷歌的WeatherNext 2，12月是美国NOAA的第一批AI全球模型。

b417f84f6802.en: So the weather became a graph problem: a mesh that wraps the planet, messages that cross it in a few steps, and diffusion for the part of the future that can't be known. Next: networks that learn whole equations.
b417f84f6802.zh: 于是天气变成了一个图问题：一个包住星球的网格网，几步就能穿过它的消息，以及为未来中无法知道的那一部分准备的扩散。接下来：学会整个方程的网络。

9dd9a22fd73f.en: Fields evolve by equations. Here is Burgers' equation, a one-dimensional cartoon of fluid flow: a wave that steepens where it is fast and is smoothed by viscosity. <bookmark mark='a'/> From this start, one time unit later, the solution looks like this. <bookmark mark='b'/> A solver needs thousands of small steps, every time. A network could learn the map from start to finish, but an ordinary one works on a fixed list of numbers: trained on sixty-four points, it knows only those. <bookmark mark='c'/> We want the operator itself, a map from functions to functions, readable at any resolution. <bookmark mark='d'/> Tianping and Hong Chen proved in 1995 that networks can approximate operators; DeepONet and the Fourier neural operator made it practical in 2021.
9dd9a22fd73f.zh: 场按方程演化。这是伯格斯方程，流体流动的一个一维漫画：一个波，在快的地方变陡，又被黏性抹平。<bookmark mark='a'/>从这个起点出发，一个时间单位之后，解是这个样子。<bookmark mark='b'/>求解器每次都要走几千个小步。一个网络可以学会从起点到终点的映射，但普通网络只处理一个固定长度的数列：用六十四个点训练，它就只认识这些点。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们要的是算子本身，一个从函数到函数的映射，在任何分辨率上都能读。<bookmark mark='d'/>陈天平和陈宏在1995年证明了网络可以逼近算子；DeepONet和傅里叶神经算子在2021年让它变得实用。

d3f4a2b728dc.en: The Fourier neural operator, from Zongyi Li, Anima Anandkumar, Andrew Stuart and colleagues, starts from a layer that is an integral: each point's new value mixes the whole field through a kernel kappa. <bookmark mark='a'/> If the kernel depends only on the offset, the integral is a convolution, which the convolution theorem makes a product of Fourier transforms. <bookmark mark='b'/> So learn the kernel's transform directly: one complex weight for each of the lowest frequencies, sixteen here, dropping the rest. <bookmark mark='c'/> The weights belong to frequencies, not grid points, so the network reads any grid fine enough to hold them; shifts pass straight through; and a layer costs about one fast Fourier transform.
d3f4a2b728dc.zh: 傅里叶神经算子出自李宗仪、阿妮玛·阿南德库马尔、安德鲁·斯图尔特等人，它从一个积分形式的网络层出发：每个点的新值，通过一个核kappa，混合了整个场。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果核只依赖于偏移量，这个积分就是一个卷积，卷积定理把它变成傅里叶变换的乘积。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以直接学核的变换：给最低的那些频率各学一个复数权重，这里是十六个，其余的丢掉。<bookmark mark='c'/>权重属于频率，不属于格点，所以网络能读任何细到足以容纳它们的网格；平移直接穿过；而一层的代价大约是一次快速傅里叶变换。

400a2b7ace16.en: We trained one on a thousand solutions of Burgers' equation, sampled at 64 points, against a pseudo-spectral solver's answers. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is its prediction for a start it never saw, at checkpoints through training, beside the learning curve. <bookmark mark='b'/> It ends with a relative error of 0.4 percent on held-out starts.
400a2b7ace16.zh: 我们用伯格斯方程的一千个解训练了一个，采样在64个点上，以一个伪谱求解器的答案为准。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是它对一个从没见过的起点的预测，在训练的各个检查点上，旁边是学习曲线。<bookmark mark='b'/>最后，它在留出的起点上的相对误差是0.4%。

ba863f215f9f.en: Now the test that matters. Both networks were trained only at sixty-four points. Read them at 32 up to 1,024. <bookmark mark='a'/> The Fourier neural operator's error stays at 0.3 percent on its own grid and 0.3 at 1,024 points, 16 times finer. <bookmark mark='b'/> The CNN, at 1.2 percent on its own grid, reaches 74 percent at the finest: its kernels, even dilated, are measured in grid points, so on a finer grid they see a narrower stretch of the line. <bookmark mark='c'/> Below its training resolution, at 32 points, the operator's error is 0.6 percent: so coarse a grid blurs the steep fronts the solution makes. FourCastNet, one of the first learned weather models, in 2022, was built on a variant of this Fourier layer.
ba863f215f9f.zh: 现在是真正要紧的测试。两个网络都只在六十四个点上训练过。从32个点到1024个点去读它们。<bookmark mark='a'/>傅里叶神经算子的误差在它自己的网格上是0.3%，在1024个点、细16倍的网格上是0.3%。<bookmark mark='b'/>CNN在它自己的网格上是1.2%，到最细的网格上变成了74%：它的核即使加了空洞，也是按格点来量的，所以在更细的网格上只能看到线上更窄的一段。<bookmark mark='c'/>在低于训练分辨率的32个点上，算子的误差是0.6%：这么粗的网格会把解形成的陡峭锋面抹平。FourCastNet是最早的学习型天气模型之一，2022年推出，它就建立在这种傅里叶层的一个变体上。

4cff16109416.en: Learn the operator, not the grid. Weights that belong to frequencies carry over to any resolution, which is what a model of the physical world should do. From fields to crystals.
4cff16109416.zh: 学算子，不学网格。属于频率的权重可以带到任何分辨率上，这正是一个物理世界的模型应该做到的。从场走向晶体。

9eb34548de94.en: Chapter fifteen. Materials by the million.

954b30113bb0.en: A crystal is a pattern of atoms repeated in space; its symmetries are one of 230 space groups, classified in 1891. Which crystals exist? <bookmark mark='a'/> Take two elements, A and B, and their possible compounds, each with a formation energy from density functional theory, hours of computer time apiece. <bookmark mark='b'/> A compound is stable if no mixture of the others has lower energy: if it lies on the lower convex hull. <bookmark mark='c'/> One above the hull would rather decompose into its neighbours; its height says how unstable it is. Here nine compounds are on the hull.
954b30113bb0.zh: 晶体是原子在空间里重复排列的图样；它的对称性属于230种空间群之一，1891年就分类完了。哪些晶体存在？<bookmark mark='a'/>取两种元素A和B，以及它们可能的化合物，每个都有一个由密度泛函理论算出的形成能，每个要花好几个小时的计算机时间。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果没有其他化合物的混合物能量更低，这个化合物就是稳定的：它落在下凸包上。<bookmark mark='c'/>在凸包上方的化合物宁愿分解成它的邻居；它的高度说明它有多不稳定。这里有9个化合物在凸包上。

e3f6bfd853ed.en: In 2023 Amil Merchant, Ekin Dogus Cubuk and colleagues at Google DeepMind published GNoME, graph networks for materials exploration. <bookmark mark='a'/> It generates candidates by swapping elements in known crystals and by random search; <bookmark mark='b'/> graph networks built on interatomic distances, and so invariant to rotation, predict their energies; <bookmark mark='c'/> density functional theory checks the most promising; <bookmark mark='d'/> and every check becomes training data for the next round. <bookmark mark='e'/> Computation had found about forty-eight thousand stable crystals; GNoME reported 2.2 million, 381,000 on the new convex hull, and the share of its picks confirmed by DFT rose above eighty percent, from about one percent before.
e3f6bfd853ed.zh: 2023年，谷歌DeepMind的阿米尔·默钱特、埃金·多古斯·丘布克等人发表了GNoME，用于材料探索的图网络。<bookmark mark='a'/>它通过替换已知晶体里的元素、以及随机搜索，来生成候选；<bookmark mark='b'/>建立在原子间距离之上、因而与转动无关的图网络，预测它们的能量；<bookmark mark='c'/>密度泛函理论检查最有希望的那些；<bookmark mark='d'/>每一次检查都变成下一轮的训练数据。<bookmark mark='e'/>此前，计算方法找到了大约四万八千种稳定晶体；GNoME报告了220万种，其中38.1万种在新的凸包上，它挑出来、被DFT确认的比例升到了百分之八十以上，而此前只有百分之一左右。

dc6aa0e0a8ce.en: We can run the flywheel on a made-up chemistry: twenty invented elements, every pair, nine compositions and four crystal types, 6,840 candidates, whose 'DFT' energy is a hidden formula revealed sixty at a time. <bookmark mark='a'/> Start knowing three percent. Each round, train a small ensemble on what is known, and check the sixty predicted to fall furthest below the hull of everything else. A hit is a pick that is truly stable. <bookmark mark='b'/> Random picks hit 12 percent of the time, about the share of stable candidates, 11 percent. <bookmark mark='c'/> The surrogate's picks hit 54 percent in the first round, rise to 62, and then fall, to 34 in the last round, as the easiest stable compounds are used up; still several times the random rate. <bookmark mark='d'/> Its error falls from 0.068 to 0.060, and after 8 rounds it has found 234 of the 780 truly stable compounds, against 78 for random picks.
dc6aa0e0a8ce.zh: 我们可以在一个虚构的化学体系上转动这个飞轮：二十种虚构的元素，两两组合，九种配比，四种晶体类型，共6840个候选，它们的“DFT”能量是一个隐藏的公式，每次只揭开六十个。<bookmark mark='a'/>一开始知道百分之三。每一轮，用已知的数据训练一个小集成模型，检查预测会落到其余一切的凸包下方最远的六十个。命中，就是挑中一个真正稳定的化合物。<bookmark mark='b'/>随机挑选的命中率是12%，大约就是稳定候选所占的比例，11%。<bookmark mark='c'/>代理模型的挑选在第一轮命中54%，升到62%，然后随着最容易找到的稳定化合物被用光而下降，最后一轮是34%；仍是随机命中率的好几倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>它的误差从0.068降到0.060，8轮之后，它找到了780个真正稳定的化合物中的234个，而随机挑选找到78个。

a9008bb2375b.en: The claims drew pushback from chemists. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2024 Anthony Cheetham and Ram Seshadri examined a random sample of GNoME's predictions and found scant evidence of compounds at once new, credible and useful; many placed atoms in neat orders that real crystals mix at random. <bookmark mark='b'/> Critics also disputed the X-ray analysis behind a robot laboratory's report of forty-one new compounds; in January 2026 the paper was corrected to thirty-six from fifty-seven targets. <bookmark mark='c'/> The tools kept improving, universal potentials and crystal generators, <bookmark mark='d'/> but the lesson stuck: a predicted crystal is a hypothesis, and making it is the test.
a9008bb2375b.zh: 这些说法遭到了化学家的质疑。<bookmark mark='a'/>2024年，安东尼·奇塔姆和拉姆·谢沙德里随机抽查了GNoME的一批预测，发现很少有证据表明其中有同时称得上新颖、可信又有用的化合物；许多预测把原子排成整齐的有序结构，而真实晶体里这些原子是随机混排的。<bookmark mark='b'/>批评者还对一个机器人实验室报告四十一种新化合物所依据的X射线分析提出了异议；2026年1月，这篇论文被更正为五十七个目标中的三十六种。<bookmark mark='c'/>工具在不断进步，通用势函数，晶体生成器，<bookmark mark='d'/>但教训留了下来：预测出来的晶体只是一个假设，把它做出来才是检验。

f3b9a01c2252.en: In materials, then, the network is a cheap first opinion that makes expensive checks count. In mathematics, the check can be perfect.
f3b9a01c2252.zh: 所以在材料领域，网络是一个便宜的初步意见，让昂贵的检查物尽其用。而在数学里，检查可以是完美的。

43f228cf345a.en: Mathematics has something no other science has: a checker that cannot be fooled. <bookmark mark='a'/> In a proof assistant such as Lean, a theorem and its proof are code, and a small kernel checks every inference; this one says that n times n plus one is even. <bookmark mark='b'/> Computers entered proofs in 1976 with Appel and Haken's four-colour theorem, which Georges Gonthier checked formally in 2005. <bookmark mark='c'/> Thomas Hales's proof of the Kepler conjecture was formally verified in 2014, <bookmark mark='d'/> and in 2022 Lean's community formalized a hard new theorem of Dustin Clausen and Peter Scholze. <bookmark mark='e'/> Lean's library, Mathlib, now holds about two hundred and ninety thousand theorems; Part 28 shows what reinforcement learning does with such a checker.
43f228cf345a.zh: 数学有一样别的科学都没有的东西：一个骗不了的检查器。<bookmark mark='a'/>在Lean这样的证明助手里，定理和证明都是代码，一个小小的内核检查每一步推理；这一个说的是，n乘以n加1是偶数。<bookmark mark='b'/>计算机进入证明是在1976年，阿佩尔和哈肯的四色定理，2005年乔治·贡蒂埃对它做了形式化检查。<bookmark mark='c'/>托马斯·黑尔斯对开普勒猜想的证明在2014年得到了形式化验证，<bookmark mark='d'/>2022年，Lean社区把达斯汀·克劳森和彼得·舒尔茨的一个困难的新定理形式化了。<bookmark mark='e'/>Lean的库Mathlib现在收录了大约二十九万条定理；第28部分会讲强化学习拿这样的检查器做了什么。

ff97da1a1daa.en: Olympiad geometry fell first. In January 2024 Trieu Trinh, Thang Luong and colleagues at Google DeepMind published AlphaGeometry. <bookmark mark='a'/> With no human proofs to learn from, they made their own: random premises, a symbolic engine deducing all that follows, and a traceback from each new fact to what it needed: a hundred million theorems with proofs. <bookmark mark='b'/> Nine percent need a point the statement never mentions, an auxiliary construction, the creative step; a language model learned to propose them, and the engine does the rest. <bookmark mark='c'/> On thirty olympiad problems it solved twenty-five, against ten for the best earlier method, fourteen for its engine alone and none for GPT-4; the average gold medallist solves 25.9. <bookmark mark='d'/> A year later AlphaGeometry 2 solved eighty-four percent of the olympiad's geometry problems since 2000.
ff97da1a1daa.zh: 奥赛几何最先被攻下。2024年1月，谷歌DeepMind的陈天如、梁明唐等人发表了AlphaGeometry。<bookmark mark='a'/>没有人类证明可学，他们就自己造：随机的前提，一个推出所有后果的符号引擎，再从每个新事实回溯到它需要的东西：一亿条带证明的定理。<bookmark mark='b'/>其中百分之九需要一个题目里从未提到的点，一条辅助构造，这是有创造性的那一步；一个语言模型学会了提出这些点，其余的交给引擎。<bookmark mark='c'/>在三十道奥赛题上，它解出了二十五道，此前最好的方法是十道，它的引擎单独是十四道，GPT-4是零道；金牌得主平均解出25.9道。<bookmark mark='d'/>一年后，AlphaGeometry 2解出了2000年以来国际数学奥林匹克几何题的百分之八十四。

34dbbef6d2ad.en: Then the olympiad itself, which Part 28 follows in detail. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2024 AlphaProof, AlphaZero's method working in Lean, with AlphaGeometry 2 for the geometry, scored twenty-eight of forty-two, one point short of gold. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2025 Google's Gemini Deep Think and an experimental OpenAI model each scored thirty-five, exactly gold, writing proofs in plain language. <bookmark mark='c'/> And in July 2026, in Shanghai, Huawei and Xiaohongshu reported perfect scores, forty-two of forty-two, with solutions submitted to the organizers for grading, as AFP reported; seven of the six hundred and sixty-six students also scored forty-two. As a test for machines, the olympiad is nearly saturated.
34dbbef6d2ad.zh: 然后是奥赛本身，第28部分会详细讲。<bookmark mark='a'/>2024年，在Lean里工作的AlphaZero方法AlphaProof，加上负责几何的AlphaGeometry 2，拿到了四十二分里的二十八分，离金牌差一分。<bookmark mark='b'/>2025年，谷歌的Gemini Deep Think和OpenAI的一个实验模型各自拿到三十五分，正好是金牌线，证明是用普通语言写的。<bookmark mark='c'/>而在2026年7月的上海，华为和小红书报告拿到了满分，四十二分里的四十二分，解答提交给了组织方评分，据法新社报道；六百六十六名学生里也有七人拿了四十二分。作为对机器的测试，奥赛已经接近饱和。

f41a2bc74edf.en: Beyond contests, the frontier is research mathematics. <bookmark mark='a'/> Autoformalization, translating informal mathematics into Lean, sped up sharply: in September 2025 the start-up Math Inc. reported that its agent Gauss had formalized the strong prime number theorem, about twenty-five thousand lines of Lean, in roughly three weeks. <bookmark mark='b'/> In January 2026 OpenAI's GPT-5.2 Pro and Harmonic's prover Aristotle resolved Erdős problem 728, with a proof that ends in Lean. <bookmark mark='c'/> A Google DeepMind team ran Gemini over seven hundred open Erdős problems: thirteen were settled, five by seemingly new arguments, eight because the answer was already in the literature. <bookmark mark='d'/> Two cautions: a formal proof proves exactly its statement, so a mistranslated statement proves the wrong thing; and the problems falling first are the easier ones.
f41a2bc74edf.zh: 在比赛之外，前沿是研究级的数学。<bookmark mark='a'/>自动形式化，也就是把非形式的数学翻译成Lean，速度猛然加快：2025年9月，初创公司Math Inc.报告说，它的智能体Gauss用大约三个星期，把强素数定理形式化了，大约两万五千行Lean代码。<bookmark mark='b'/>2026年1月，OpenAI的GPT-5.2 Pro和Harmonic的证明器Aristotle解决了埃尔德什第728号问题，最后给出的是一个Lean证明。<bookmark mark='c'/>谷歌DeepMind的一个团队让Gemini处理了七百个未解的埃尔德什问题：解决了十三个，五个靠的是看来是新的论证，八个是因为答案原来已经在文献里了。<bookmark mark='d'/>两点提醒：形式化证明恰好证明它的陈述，所以译错的陈述证明的是错的东西；而且最先被攻下的都是比较容易的问题。

f5fd631b49fc.en: With a perfect checker, search can be trusted: generate freely, keep only what checks. The last chapter is about exactly that.
f5fd631b49fc.zh: 有了完美的检查器，搜索就可以信任：放手去生成，只留下通过检查的。最后一章讲的正是这个。

342957764452.en: When the checker is exact, discovery becomes a loop. <bookmark mark='a'/> Propose a candidate, a program or a construction; <bookmark mark='b'/> score it exactly; <bookmark mark='c'/> keep the best and vary them. <bookmark mark='d'/> AlphaTensor, in 2022, used an AlphaZero network as the proposer.
