In December 2023 FunSearch, from Bernardino Romera-Paredes and colleagues at Google DeepMind, made the proposer a language model writing Python, with programs kept on separate islands like populations in evolution. <bookmark mark='e'/> It found a cap set in eight dimensions, five hundred and twelve points with no three in a line, beating the four hundred and ninety-six known.
342957764452.zh: 当检查器是精确的，发现就变成了一个循环。<bookmark mark='a'/>提出一个候选，一段程序或一个构造；<bookmark mark='b'/>精确地给它打分；<bookmark mark='c'/>留下最好的，再变化它们。<bookmark mark='d'/>2022年的AlphaTensor用一个AlphaZero网络来提出候选。2023年12月，谷歌DeepMind的贝尔纳迪诺·罗梅拉-帕雷德斯等人的FunSearch把提出者换成了一个写Python的语言模型，程序放在彼此分开的岛上，就像进化中的种群。<bookmark mark='e'/>它在八维空间里找到了一个帽集，五百一十二个点，没有三点共线，超过了已知的四百九十六个。

510d726dc068.en: Let's run that loop ourselves, on one of FunSearch's problems: online bin packing. <bookmark mark='a'/> Items arrive one at a time, and each must go into a bin at once. A rule decides: score every bin the item fits in, and pick the highest. <bookmark mark='b'/> The classic is best fit: the bin with the least room left. <bookmark mark='c'/> We evolve such scores as formulas, with random mutations and crossings standing in for the language model, judged by how many bins they use on eight training sequences. Within 39 generations it beats best fit on its training instances by 0.41 points. <bookmark mark='d'/> On new, longer sequences of items, both evolved rules still beat best fit: 4.11 and 4.29 percent against 4.71. <bookmark mark='e'/> Ours carried over; but an independent study in 2025 found that heuristics evolved by language models often don't generalize beyond the instances they were bred on.
510d726dc068.zh: 我们自己来跑这个循环，用FunSearch的一个问题：在线装箱。<bookmark mark='a'/>物品一个一个到来，每个都必须立刻放进一个箱子。一条规则来决定：给物品放得下的每个箱子打分，挑分最高的。<bookmark mark='b'/>经典的规则是最佳适配：挑剩余空间最小的箱子。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们把这样的打分当作公式来进化，用随机的变异和交叉代替语言模型，按它们在八个训练序列上用了多少箱子来评判。39代之内，它在训练实例上比最佳适配好0.41个百分点。<bookmark mark='d'/>在新的、更长的物品序列上，两条进化出来的规则仍然都胜过最佳适配：4.11%和4.29%，对4.71%。<bookmark mark='e'/>我们的规则迁移过去了；不过2025年的一项独立研究发现，语言模型进化出来的启发式方法常常无法推广到培育它们的那些实例之外。

c72780da8b57.en: Matrix multiplication is the purest case. <bookmark mark='a'/> The schoolbook way to multiply two n by n matrices uses n cubed multiplications. <bookmark mark='b'/> Write the product as a three-way tensor; <bookmark mark='c'/> then every way of writing that tensor as a sum of R simple products is an algorithm with R multiplications. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 1969 Volker Strassen found seven for two by two matrices, not eight, and Shmuel Winograd proved two years later that seven is the minimum. <bookmark mark='e'/> We searched for these decompositions numerically, from thirty random starts at each rank. At rank six, none of the 30 starts gets below an error of 0.35: there is no six-multiplication algorithm to find. At rank seven, 29 of 30 starts find one: a Strassen-like algorithm, which multiplies random matrices correctly to 7 decimal places. <bookmark mark='f'/> For three by three matrices the record, Julian Laderman's from 1976, is twenty-three multiplications; from 10 starts at that rank, and as many at twenty-six, our search got within about a millionth of zero but never exactly there: as the matrices grow, exact decompositions become needles in a haystack.
c72780da8b57.zh: 矩阵乘法是最纯粹的例子。<bookmark mark='a'/>按教科书的方法，两个n乘n矩阵相乘要做n的三次方次乘法。<bookmark mark='b'/>把这个乘积写成一个三向张量；<bookmark mark='c'/>那么，把这个张量写成R个简单乘积之和的每一种写法，都是一个只用R次乘法的算法。<bookmark mark='d'/>1969年，福尔克尔·施特拉森为二乘二矩阵找到了七次的算法，而不是八次；两年后，什穆埃尔·维诺格拉德证明了七就是最少的。<bookmark mark='e'/>我们用数值方法搜索这些分解，每个秩从三十个随机起点出发。At rank six, none of the 30 starts gets below an error of 0。35: there is no six-multiplication algorithm to find. At rank seven, 29 of 30 starts find one: a Strassen-like algorithm, which multiplies random matrices correctly to 7 decimal places。<bookmark mark='f'/>对三乘三矩阵，纪录是朱利安·拉德曼1976年给出的二十三次乘法；在这个秩上从10个起点出发，在二十六上也一样多，我们的搜索离零只差大约百万分之一，却始终没有精确到零：矩阵一变大，精确的分解就成了大海里的针。

78748483ddde.en: In May 2025 Google DeepMind combined both lines in AlphaEvolve. <bookmark mark='a'/> Gemini models propose changes to whole programs, evaluators score them, and evolution keeps the best. <bookmark mark='b'/> Among its results: four by four complex matrices multiplied with forty-eight multiplications, beating the forty-nine of applying Strassen's trick twice, the record since 1969, <bookmark mark='c'/> found by evolving a decomposition search like ours. <bookmark mark='d'/> Within weeks, three researchers in France found a forty-eight with rational coefficients. <bookmark mark='e'/> It also raised to 593 the number of spheres that can touch a central one in eleven dimensions, and on over fifty open problems matched the best known answer in three quarters and improved it in a fifth. <bookmark mark='f'/> Inside Google, a scheduling rule it found recovers 0.7 percent of the company's computing. <bookmark mark='g'/> In November 2025 Terence Tao and colleagues tried it on sixty-seven problems, and published its failures too.
78748483ddde.zh: 2025年5月，谷歌DeepMind在AlphaEvolve里把两条路线结合了起来。<bookmark mark='a'/>Gemini模型对整段程序提出修改，评估器给它们打分，进化留下最好的。<bookmark mark='b'/>它的成果之一：用四十八次乘法完成四乘四复矩阵的乘法，打破了把施特拉森的技巧用两次得到的四十九次，那是1969年以来的纪录，<bookmark mark='c'/>靠的是进化一个像我们这样的分解搜索。<bookmark mark='d'/>几个星期之内，法国的三位研究者找到了一个系数为有理数的四十八次方案。<bookmark mark='e'/>它还把十一维空间里能与中心球相切的球数提高到593个；在五十多个未解问题上，四分之三追平了已知最好的答案，五分之一改进了它。<bookmark mark='f'/>在谷歌内部，它找到的一条调度规则收回了公司0.7%的算力。<bookmark mark='g'/>2025年11月，陶哲轩等人在六十七个问题上试用了它，连失败也一并发表了。

1029d85348d4.en: Discovery by search, then: propose freely, check exactly, keep what survives. It works wherever the checking is exact, which is why mathematics and algorithms went first.
1029d85348d4.zh: 所以，靠搜索做发现：放手去提出，精确地检查，留下经得起检查的。只要检查是精确的，它就管用，这就是数学和算法走在最前面的原因。

3b7b63ef3571.en: Let's take stock. A symmetry is a transformation that shouldn't change the answer; a network can respect it exactly, by construction, or approximately, from examples. Sums make functions of sets; sums over neighbours make graph networks, which see what colour refinement sees and blur when stacked deep. Built-in rotations made our molecule model far better on the same data. AlphaFold reads a protein through pairs kept consistent by triangles, builds it from frames, and scores it with a loss that knows left from right; its successor hands the atoms to diffusion. Weather runs on a mesh, equations are learned as operators, crystals are screened by the million, and where the checker is perfect, search discovers.
3b7b63ef3571.zh: 我们来盘点一下。对称是一个不应该改变答案的变换；网络可以精确地尊重它，靠构造；也可以近似地尊重它，靠例子。求和构成集合上的函数；对邻居求和构成图网络，它看见的正是颜色细化看见的，叠得太深就会变模糊。内置转动让我们的分子模型在同样的数据上好得多。AlphaFold通过用三角形保持一致的残基对来读蛋白质，用坐标系把它搭起来，再用一个分得清左右的损失来打分；它的后继者把原子交给了扩散。天气在网格网上运行，方程被当作算子来学，晶体按百万量级筛选，而在检查器完美的地方，搜索带来发现。

ac57e441065f.en: All of this comes back. <bookmark mark='a'/> Search guided by a network and judged by an exact checker is AlphaZero, next time, and Part 28's reasoning models. <bookmark mark='b'/> A learned simulator that rolls the world forward, like our mesh network, is Part 29's world model. <bookmark mark='c'/> What a network's layers represent, and whether they respect the symmetries we expect, is Part 30's subject. <bookmark mark='d'/> And CASP's blind tests and a nearly saturated olympiad lead to Part 31's question: how to evaluate at all.
ac57e441065f.zh: 这一切都还会再出现。<bookmark mark='a'/>由网络引导、由精确检查器评判的搜索，就是下一次的AlphaZero，以及第28部分的推理模型。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个把世界向前推演的学习型模拟器，就像我们的网格网络，就是第29部分的世界模型。<bookmark mark='c'/>网络的各层表示了什么，它们是否尊重我们期望的对称，是第30部分的主题。<bookmark mark='d'/>而CASP的盲测和一个几乎饱和的奥赛，引向第31部分的问题：到底该怎样评估。

a85eed5a2c5b.en: Here are six problems to try, from equivariant compositions to the Fourier layer. Pause here and work through them; full solutions are in this part's notes.
a85eed5a2c5b.zh: 这里有六道习题，从等变映射的复合到傅里叶层。在这里暂停一下，动手做一做；完整的解答在本部分的讲义里。

9b75212777d6.en: Next time, the fifth act: agency. The search loop of this chapter, propose, check, keep the best, becomes learning from reward: an agent acts, the world answers, and the agent improves, all the way to AlphaZero, which we will train ourselves. Part 26: reinforcement learning, from Bellman to AlphaZero.
9b75212777d6.zh: 下一次，第五幕：能动性。本章的搜索循环，提出、检查、保留最好的，变成了从奖励中学习：智能体行动，世界给出回应，智能体不断改进，一直到AlphaZero，我们会亲手训练一个。第26部分：强化学习，从贝尔曼到AlphaZero。

156efedaf81b.en: To go deeper, Bronstein, Bruna, Cohen and Veličković's book on geometric deep learning is the map of this whole part, and William Hamilton's short book covers graph networks clearly. Thanks for watching, and see you in Part 26.
156efedaf81b.zh: 想深入了解，布朗斯坦、布鲁纳、科恩和韦利奇科维奇关于几何深度学习的书是整个这一部分的地图，威廉·汉密尔顿的小书把图网络讲得很清楚。感谢收看，我们第26部分再见。
